title.zh: 卷二百六十五 列傳第二十四 李昉 呂蒙正 張齊賢 賈黃中
title.en: Volume 265 Biographies 24: Li Fang, Lu Mengzheng, Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong
title.raw: 卷二百六十五 列傳第二十四 李昉 呂蒙正 張齊賢 賈黃中 Volume 265 Biographies 24: Li Fang, Lu Mengzheng, Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong

sentences.zh: 李昉，字明遠，深州饒陽人。

translations.literal: Li Fang, style name Mingyuan, was a man of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang, whose style was Mingyuan, came from Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父起，晉工部郎中、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: His father Qi was a bureau director in the Ministry of Works under Jin and a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi had served under the Jin as a director in the Ministry of Works and as a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 從大父右資善大夫超無子，以昉為後，蔭補齋郎，選授太子校書。

translations.literal: His great-uncle by the mother's side, the Right Virtuous Grandee Chao, had no son, so Fang was made his heir; through inherited privilege he was made a qi lang, and through selection was appointed collator to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's uncle, Chao, who held the title Right Virtuous Grandee, had no son, so Fang was adopted as his heir. Through hereditary privilege he received appointment as a qi lang, and by selection he became collator to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐舉進士，為秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han he passed the jinshi examination and became a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou reign of the Later Han he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary.

sentences.zh: 宰相馮道引之，與呂端同直弘文館，改右拾遺、集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: Chancellor Feng Dao recommended him; together with Lü Duan he served in the Hongwen Pavilion, and he was changed to Right Reminder and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Feng Dao brought him forward; he served in the Hongwen Pavilion alongside Lü Duan, then was promoted to Right Reminder and compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 周顯德二年，宰相李穀征淮南，昉為記室。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande of Zhou, Chancellor Li Gu campaigned in Huainan, and Fang served as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiande under the Later Zhou, Chancellor Li Gu marched against Huainan, and Fang served as his recorder.

sentences.zh: 世宗覽軍中章奏，愛其辭理明白，已知為昉所作，及見《相國寺文英院集》，乃昉與扈蒙、崔頌、劉袞、竇儼、趙逢及昉弟載所題，益善昉詩而稱賞之曰：「吾久知有此人矣。」

translations.literal: Shizong reviewed memorials from the army, admired their clear reasoning, and already knew they were written by Fang; when he saw the Collected Works of the Wenyin Academy at Xiangguo Temple, which Fang together with Hu Meng, Cui Song, Liu Gun, Dou Yan, Zhao Feng, and Fang's younger brother Zai had inscribed, he admired Fang's poetry still more and praised him, saying: "I have long known there was such a person."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong read the army's memorials, admired their lucid argument, and already knew Fang had written them. When he saw the Collected Works of the Wenyin Academy at Xiangguo Temple—inscribed by Fang together with Hu Meng, Cui Song, Liu Gun, Dou Yan, Zhao Feng, and Fang's younger brother Zai—he admired Fang's poetry all the more and exclaimed, "I have long known such a man existed."

sentences.zh: 師還，擢為主客員外郎、知制誥、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Receptions, drafter of edicts, and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Receptions, made drafter of edicts, and appointed direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 四年，加史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was additionally made compiler of the Historiography Institute and given charge of its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was also made a compiler of the Historiography Institute and put in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，世宗南征，從至高郵，會陶穀出使，內署書詔填委，乃命為屯田郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: That winter Shizong campaigned south; Fang accompanied him to Gaoyou. When Tao Gu went on a mission, the inner secretariat was flooded with edicts to draft, so he was appointed director of the Bureau of State Farms and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Shizong marched south, Fang accompanied him as far as Gaoyou. Tao Gu was away on a mission, and the inner secretariat was overwhelmed with edicts to draft, so Fang was appointed director of the Bureau of State Farms and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 六年春，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year he mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, he was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Fang was granted the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made Grandee of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was promoted to Grandee of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，罷為給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was dismissed and made Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he was removed from office and appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，平湖湘，受詔祀南嶽，就命知衡州，逾年代歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Hunan was pacified, he received orders to sacrifice at the Southern Sacred Peak; on the spot he was appointed prefect of Hengzhou, and after his term expired he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after Hunan was pacified, he was ordered to perform sacrifices at Mount Heng. He was appointed on the spot to govern Hengzhou, and returned when his term ended.

sentences.zh: 陶穀誣奏昉為所親求京畿令，上怒，召吏部尚書張昭面質其事。

translations.literal: Tao Gu falsely memorialized that Fang had sought a magistracy in the capital region for a relative; the emperor was angry and summoned Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao to confront him on the matter face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Gu falsely accused Fang of seeking a capital-region magistracy for a kinsman. The emperor was furious and summoned Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao to confront the charge in person.

sentences.zh: 昭老儒氣直，免冠上前，抗聲云：「穀罔上。」

translations.literal: Zhao, an old Confucian, was upright in spirit; removing his cap he stepped before the throne and spoke boldly: "Gu deceived the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, an elderly Confucian of blunt integrity, doffed his cap, stepped forward, and declared in a loud voice, "Gu has deceived Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上疑之不釋，出昉為彰武軍行軍司馬，居延州，為生業以老。

translations.literal: The emperor remained doubtful and did not release the matter; Fang was sent out as acting marshal of Zhangwu Army, residing in Yanzhou, where he made his livelihood in his old age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained unconvinced and did not drop the case. Fang was sent out as acting marshal of the Zhangwu army and lived at Yanzhou, supporting himself in retirement.

sentences.zh: 三歲當內徙，昉不願。

translations.literal: After three years he was due to be moved inward, but Fang did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was due for reassignment inland, but Fang did not want to leave.

sentences.zh: 宰相薦其可大用，開寶二年，召還，復拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: The chancellor recommended that he could be greatly used; in the second year of Kaibao he was summoned back and again appointed Grandee of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor recommended him as fit for high office. In the second year of Kaibao he was recalled and again made Grandee of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，直學士院。

translations.literal: Before long he served directly in the Academy of Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was assigned to serve directly in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三年，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year he supervised the imperial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as chief examiner for the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 五年，復知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again supervised the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again presided over the examinations.

sentences.zh: 秋，預宴大明殿，上見昉坐盧多遜下，因問宰相，對曰：「多遜學士，昉直殿爾。」

translations.literal: In autumn he attended a banquet in the Great Bright Hall; the emperor saw Fang seated below Lu Duosun and asked the chancellor, who answered: "Duosun is an academician; Fang merely serves in the hall."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, at a banquet in the Hall of Great Brightness, the emperor noticed Fang seated below Lu Duosun and asked the chancellor why. The chancellor replied, "Duosun holds the title of academician; Fang only serves in the hall."

sentences.zh: 即令真拜學士，令居多遜上。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered him truly appointed academician and seated above Duosun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered Fang formally appointed academician and seated above Duosun.

sentences.zh: 昉之知貢舉也，其鄉人武濟川預選，既而奏對失次，昉坐左遷太常少卿，俄判國子監。

translations.literal: When Fang supervised the examinations, his fellow townsman Wu Jichuan was among those selected; later Wu's court audience was out of order, and Fang was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices, and soon afterward was made director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: While Fang was chief examiner, his fellow townsman Wu Jichuan was among the candidates chosen. Later Wu blundered in his palace audience, and Fang was demoted to vice director of the Court of Sacrifices, then soon put in charge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，復拜中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he was again appointed Grandee of the Secretariat and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year he was again made Grandee of the Secretariat and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 冬，判吏部銓。

translations.literal: In winter he was put in charge of the Board of Civil Office selections.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was assigned to oversee personnel selection at the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 時趙普為多遜所構，數以其短聞於上，上詢於昉，對曰：「臣職司書詔，普之所為，非臣所知。」

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Pu was framed by Duosun, who several times reported his faults to the emperor; the emperor inquired of Fang, who answered: "My office is to draft edicts; what Pu does is not known to me."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Pu was undermined by Duosun, who repeatedly reported his faults to the throne. When the emperor asked Fang, he replied, "My duty is to draft edicts; I do not know what Pu has been doing."

sentences.zh: 普尋出鎮，多遜遂參知政事。

translations.literal: Pu was soon sent out to command a prefecture, and Duosun became Associate Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu was soon sent out to govern a military prefecture, and Duosun became associate administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年郊祀，命昉與琪並為左右僕射，昉固辭，乃加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: For the suburban sacrifice in the first year of Yongxi, Fang and Qi were both appointed Left and Right Vice Directors, but Fang firmly declined and was instead made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For the Yongxi suburban sacrifice, Fang and Qi were both named left and right vice directors, but Fang firmly declined and was made vice director of the Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 王師討幽薊不利，遣使分詣河南、東，籍民為兵，凡八丁取一。

translations.literal: When the imperial army's campaign against You and Ji went badly, envoys were sent to Henan and the east to register the people as soldiers, taking one man from every eight households.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against You and Ji faltered, envoys were dispatched to Henan and the eastern circuits to register civilians as soldiers, drafting one man from every eight households.

sentences.zh: 昉等相率奏曰：「近者分遣使籍河南、東四十餘郡之民以為邊備，非得已也。

translations.literal: Fang and the others jointly memorialized, saying: "Recently envoys were sent to register the people of more than forty commanderies in Henan and the east for frontier defense—this could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his colleagues jointly submitted a memorial: "Envoys have lately been sent to register the people of more than forty commanderies in Henan and the east for frontier defense. The measure was unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 然河南之民素習農桑，罔知戰鬥，一旦括集，必致動搖，若因而嘯聚，更須剪除。

translations.literal: Yet the people of Henan have long been accustomed to farming and mulberry culture and know nothing of battle; once they are rounded up and gathered, unrest is sure to follow, and if they then gather in rebellion, still more cutting down will be needed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people of Henan have long practiced farming and sericulture and know nothing of war. Once they are rounded up, turmoil is inevitable; if they rise in bands, still more bloodshed will follow.

sentences.zh: 如此，則河北閭閻既困於戎馬，河南生聚復擾於萑蒲，矧當春和，有妨農作。

translations.literal: Thus the villages of Hebei will already be worn down by war-horses, while the living masses of Henan will again be disturbed by brambles and reeds; moreover, it is now spring, when farming ought not to be hindered.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei will already be exhausted by war-horses, while Henan's population will again be harried by rebellion—and all this at the height of spring, when the plough should not be idle.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以明詔既頒，難於反汗，則當續遣使臣，嚴加戒飭，所至點募，人情若有不安，即須少緩，密奏取裁，庶免後患。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty finds it hard to go back on a clear edict already issued, then additional envoys should be sent with strict instructions: wherever conscription is carried out, if the people show any unease, the matter must be eased somewhat and reported in secret for the throne's decision, so that later troubles may be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty feels bound by an edict already promulgated, send further envoys with stern instructions: wherever levies are made, if the people show distress, ease the burden and report secretly for imperial decision, so that later troubles may be averted."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and adopted their advice.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，布衣翟馬周擊登聞鼓，訟昉居宰相位，當北方有事之時，不為邊備，徒知賦詩宴樂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, the commoner Zhai Mazhou struck the Denunciation Drum, accusing Fang of holding the post of chancellor when affairs in the north were urgent yet making no frontier preparations, knowing only how to compose poetry and feast.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong era, a commoner named Zhai Mazhou beat the Denunciation Drum, charging that Fang, though chief minister, had made no frontier preparations while the north was in crisis and had done nothing but write poetry and hold banquets.

sentences.zh: 屬耤田禮方畢，乃詔學士賈黃中草制，罷昉為右僕射，且加切責。

translations.literal: The ploughing ceremony had just been completed, so the emperor ordered Academician Jia Huangzhong to draft an edict demoting Fang to Right Vice Director and adding a stern rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The ploughing rite had just concluded, and the emperor ordered Academician Jia Huangzhong to draft an edict demoting Fang to right vice director with a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 黃中言：「僕射，百僚師長，實宰相之任，今自工部尚書而遷是職，非黜責也。

translations.literal: Huangzhong said: "The vice director is the teacher of the hundred officials and in reality holds the chancellor's charge; to move him from Minister of Works to this post is not a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong argued: "The vice director is mentor to the hundred officials and in substance holds a chancellor's duties. To move him from Minister of Works to this office is no disgrace.

sentences.zh: 若曰文昌務簡，以均勞逸為辭，斯為得體。」

translations.literal: If it is said that the Secretariat's affairs are to be simplified and labor shared for balance, that would be fitting in form."
translations.idiomatic: If the edict speaks of easing the Secretariat's burdens and sharing the toil for balance, that would be proper in tone."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 會邊警益急，詔文武群臣各進策備禦，昉又引漢、唐故事，深以屈己修好、弭兵息民為言，時論稱之。

translations.literal: As frontier alarms grew more urgent, the emperor ordered civil and military officials each to submit plans for defense; Fang again cited Han and Tang precedents, urging humbling oneself to restore good relations, cease arms, and give the people rest, and contemporaries praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As border alarms intensified, the court ordered civil and military officials to submit defense plans. Fang again drew on Han and Tang precedents, urging humility, renewed peace, and respite for the people, and won praise from his peers.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，復以本官兼中書侍郎、平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he again held his former office while also serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, and supervising compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he again held his former rank while also serving as vice director of the Secretariat, grand councillor, and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，旱蝗，既雨。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year there was drought and locusts; after rain came.
translations.idiomatic: In the third summer drought and locusts struck; then rain fell.

sentences.zh: 時昉與張齊賢、賈黃中、李沆同居宰輔，以燮理非材，上表待罪，上不之罪。

translations.literal: At that time Fang, together with Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong, and Li Hang, shared the chief ministership; deeming themselves unfit to harmonize governance, they submitted memorials asking to be punished, but the emperor did not blame them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then shared power with Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong, and Li Hang. Judging themselves unfit to harmonize the state, they asked to be punished; the emperor did not reproach them.

sentences.zh: 四年，昉以私門連遭憂戚，求解機務，詔不允，遣齊賢等諭旨，復起視事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Fang, because his household had suffered repeated bereavements, asked to be relieved of key duties; the edict did not permit it, and Qi Xian and others were sent to convey the imperial will and urge him to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Fang, his family stricken by repeated mourning, asked to leave high office. The throne refused; Zhang Qixian and others were sent to convey the imperial will and urge him back to duty.

sentences.zh: 後數月，罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: Several months later he was dismissed as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was removed as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 先是，上召張洎草制，授昉左僕射，罷相，洎言：「昉居燮理之任，而陰陽乖戾，不能決意引退，俾居百僚師長之任，何以示勸？」

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had summoned Zhang Bi to draft an edict appointing Fang Left Vice Director and removing him from the chancellorship; Bi said: "Fang held the charge of harmonizing governance, yet yin and yang were out of joint and he would not resolve to withdraw—how can he be set over the hundred officials as their teacher and still serve as encouragement?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had Zhang Bi draft an edict making Fang left vice director and removing him from the chancellorship. Bi objected: "Fang held the charge of harmonizing the state, yet heaven and earth were out of balance and he would not step down—how can he stand as teacher to the hundred officials and still be held up as an example?"

sentences.zh: 上覽奏，乃令罷守本官。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial, he ordered Fang to leave office but keep his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Bi's memorial, the emperor ordered Fang dismissed from high office but allowed to keep his original rank.

sentences.zh: 晉侍中崧者，與昉同宗且同里，時人謂崧為東李家，昉為西李家。

translations.literal: The Jin Palace Attendant Song and Fang were of the same clan and the same village; people of the time called Song the Li family of the east and Fang the Li family of the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin palace attendant Song was Fang's clansman and fellow townsman; contemporaries called Song the eastern Li family and Fang the western Li family.

sentences.zh: 漢末，崧被誅。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Song was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Later Han, Song was put to death.

sentences.zh: 至是，其子璨自蘇州常熟縣令赴調，昉為訟其父冤，且言：「周太祖已為昭雪贈官，還其田宅，錄璨而官之。

translations.literal: By then his son Can had come from Changshu in Suzhou to take up an appointment; Fang pleaded his father's injustice and said: "Emperor Taizu of Zhou had already cleared his name, granted posthumous office, restored his fields and houses, and enrolled Can for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: By then Song's son Can had come up from his post as magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou. Fang pleaded his kinsman's innocence, noting that Emperor Taizu of Zhou had already cleared Song's name, granted posthumous rank, restored his lands and house, and enrolled Can for office.

sentences.zh: 然璨年幾五十，尚淹州縣之職，臣昔與之同難，豈宜叨遇聖明。

translations.literal: Yet Can is nearly fifty and still lingers in prefectural and county posts; I once shared his hardship—how can I accept such favor under a sage reign?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Can is nearly fifty and still stuck in county office. I once shared his misfortune—how can I accept such favor under a sage reign?

sentences.zh: 儻推一視之仁，澤及衰微之祚，則已往之冤獲伸於下，而繼絕之恩永光簡冊矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty extends a single glance of kindness to reach a declining line, then past wrongs will be redressed below and the grace of continuing a severed lineage will shine forever in the annals."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty extends one impartial kindness to a fallen house, past wrongs will be righted below and the grace of continuing a severed line will shine forever in the records.

sentences.zh: 詔授璨著作佐郎，後官至右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Can Assistant Compiler, and he later rose to Right Director of the Court of Appanages.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Can assistant compiler; he later reached right director of the Court of Appanages.

sentences.zh: 二年，陪祀南郊，禮畢入賀，因拜舞仆地，臺吏掖之以出，臥疾數日薨，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second year he accompanied the southern suburban sacrifice; when the rites ended and he entered to offer congratulations, he bowed and collapsed; clerks of the censorate helped him out; after several days of illness he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he attended the southern suburban sacrifice. After the rites he entered to offer congratulations, bowed, and collapsed. Censorate clerks helped him out; he lay ill several days and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Wenzheng, "Cultivated Uprightness."

sentences.zh: 昉和厚多恕，不念舊惡，在位小心循謹，無赫赫稱。

translations.literal: Fang was mild and generous, bearing no grudges; in office he was cautious and scrupulous, without striking renown.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was gentle, tolerant, and slow to remember old slights. In office he was careful and scrupulous, winning no dazzling reputation.

sentences.zh: 為文章慕白居易，尤淺近易曉。

translations.literal: In writing he admired Bai Juyi, especially favoring what was plain and easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he took Bai Juyi as his model, especially favoring language that was plain and readily understood.

sentences.zh: 好接賓客，江南平，士大夫歸朝者多從之遊。

translations.literal: He loved receiving guests; after the south was pacified, many scholar-officials returning to court associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in entertaining guests; after the south was pacified, many scholar-officials returning to court sought his company.

sentences.zh: 雅厚張洎而薄張佖，及昉罷相，洎草制深攻詆之，而佖朔望必詣昉。

translations.literal: He favored Zhang Bi warmly but looked coldly on Zhang Yi; when Fang left the chancellorship, Bi's drafted edict attacked him harshly, yet Yi visited Fang every new and full moon without fail.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zhang Bi warmly but Zhang Yi coldly. When Fang left office, Bi's edict attacked him bitterly, yet Yi called on Fang at every new and full moon without fail.

sentences.zh: 或謂佖曰：「李公待君素不厚，何數詣之？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Yi: "Master Li has never treated you well—why do you visit him so often?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Yi, "Master Li has never favored you—why do you visit so often?"

sentences.zh: 佖曰：「我為廷尉日，李公方秉政，未嘗一有請求，此吾所以重之也。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "When I was commandant of the court, Master Li held power and never once made a request of me—that is why I respect him."
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "When I was commandant of the court, Master Li held power and never once asked me for a favor—that is why I esteem him."

sentences.zh: 昉所居有園亭別墅之勝，多召故人親友宴樂其中。

translations.literal: Where Fang lived there were gardens, pavilions, and villas of fine scenery; he often summoned old friends and kin to feast and enjoy themselves there.
translations.idiomatic: His residence boasted gardens, pavilions, and villas of rare beauty, and he often gathered old friends and kin for feasting there.

sentences.zh: 既致政，欲尋洛中九老故事，時吏部尚書宋琪年七十九，左諫議大夫楊徽之年七十五，郢州刺史魏丕年七十六，太常少卿致仕李運年八十，水部郎中朱昂年七十一，廬州節度副使武允成年七十九，太子中允致仕張好問年八十五，吳僧讚寧年七十八，議將集，會蜀寇而罷。

translations.literal: After he retired from office he wished to revive the story of the Nine Elders of Luoyang; at that time Minister of Personnel Song Qi was seventy-nine, Left Reminder Yang Weizhi seventy-five, Prefect of Ying Wei Pi seventy-six, retired Vice Director of Sacrifices Li Yun eighty, Director of Waterways Zhu Ang seventy-one, Deputy Military Commissioner of Luzhou Wu Yuncheng seventy-nine, retired Palace Attendant Zhang Haowen eighty-five, the Wu monk Zanning seventy-eight—they were about to assemble when bandits in Shu caused the plan to be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he hoped to revive the Nine Elders of Luoyang. Song Qi, minister of personnel, was seventy-nine; Yang Weizhi, left reminder, seventy-five; Wei Pi, prefect of Ying, seventy-six; Li Yun, retired vice director of sacrifices, eighty; Zhu Ang, director of waterways, seventy-one; Wu Yuncheng, deputy commissioner of Luzhou, seventy-nine; Zhang Haowen, retired palace attendant, eighty-five; the Wu monk Zanning, seventy-eight. They were about to gather when unrest in Shu forced the plan to be dropped.

sentences.zh: 昉素與盧多遜善，待之不疑，多遜屢譖昉於上，或以告昉，不之信。

translations.literal: Fang had long been on good terms with Lu Duosun and trusted him without doubt; Duosun repeatedly slandered Fang to the emperor, and though some told Fang, he did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had long been close to Lu Duosun and trusted him without reserve. Duosun repeatedly slandered Fang to the throne, and though others warned him, Fang would not believe it.

sentences.zh: 及入相，太宗言及多遜事，昉頗為解釋。

translations.literal: When he entered the chancellorship, Taizong spoke of Duosun's conduct, and Fang offered considerable explanation in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang became chief minister, Taizong spoke of Duosun's conduct, and Fang offered a good deal of explanation in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「多遜居常毀卿一錢不直。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Duosun in ordinary times said you were not worth a cash."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Duosun used to say you were not worth a single cash."

sentences.zh: 昉始信之。

translations.literal: Only then did Fang believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Fang believe it.

sentences.zh: 上由此益重昉。

translations.literal: From this the emperor esteemed Fang all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor esteemed Fang all the more.

sentences.zh: 昉居中書日，有求進用者，雖知其材可取，必正色拒絕之，已而擢用；

translations.literal: While Fang was in the Secretariat, if someone sought advancement, though he knew the man's talent was acceptable he would sternly refuse; afterward he would promote him.
translations.idiomatic: While Fang held office in the Secretariat, if someone sought promotion and he judged the man fit, he would refuse him sternly—then promote him later.

sentences.zh: 或不足用，必和顏溫語待之。

translations.literal: If the man was not fit for use, he would receive him with a gentle countenance and warm words.
translations.idiomatic: If the man was unfit, he would meet him with a gentle face and kind words.

sentences.zh: 子弟問其故，曰：「用賢，人主之事；

translations.literal: His sons asked the reason; he said: "Employing the worthy is the ruler's affair.
translations.idiomatic: His sons asked why. He said, "Employing the worthy is the ruler's affair.

sentences.zh: 若受其請，是市私恩也，故峻絕之，使恩歸於上。

translations.literal: If one accepts their request, that is trading private favor; therefore I refuse them sternly so that the favor returns to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: To accept their plea is to trade in private favor, so I refuse them harshly and let the credit belong to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若不用者，既失所望，又無善辭，取怨之道也。」

translations.literal: If they are not employed, having lost what they hoped for and having no kind words, that is the way to incur resentment."
translations.idiomatic: If they are not employed, they have lost what they hoped for and received no gracious reply—that is how resentment is bred."

sentences.zh: 初，超未有子，昉母謝方娠，指腹謂伯母張曰：「生男當與伯母為子。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chao had no son, Fang's mother Xie was pregnant; pointing at her belly she told her sister-in-law Zhang: "If it is a boy, he shall be your son."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chao had no son, Fang's mother Xie was pregnant. Pointing at her belly she told her sister-in-law Zhang, "If this is a boy, he shall be yours."

sentences.zh: 故昉出繼於超。

translations.literal: Therefore Fang was given in adoption to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Fang was given in adoption to Chao.

sentences.zh: 昉再相，因表其事，求贈所生父母官。

translations.literal: When Fang became chancellor a second time, he memorialized stating the matter and asked that posthumous offices be granted to his birth parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang became chancellor again, he memorialized on the matter and asked posthumous rank for his birth parents.

sentences.zh: 詔贈其祖溫太子太傅，祖母權氏莒國太夫人，起太子太師，謝氏鄭國太夫人。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made his grandfather Wen Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, his grandmother Lady Quan Grand Lady of Ju, Qi Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and Lady Xie Grand Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made his grandfather Wen grand preceptor of the crown prince, his grandmother Lady Quan grand lady of Ju, his father Qi grand preceptor of the crown prince, and Lady Xie grand lady of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 昉素病心悸，數歲一發，發必彌年而後愈，蓋典誥命三十餘年，勞役思慮所致。

translations.literal: Fang had long suffered palpitations of the heart; every few years it would flare up, and when it flared it would last a full year before he recovered—this came from drafting edicts for more than thirty years and the strain of labor and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had long suffered heart palpitations; every few years they would flare, and each flare lasted a full year before he recovered—thirty years of drafting edicts and the strain of anxious labor were the cause.

sentences.zh: 及居相位，益加憂畏。

translations.literal: When he reached the chancellorship his anxiety and fear increased still more.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the chancellorship, his anxiety only deepened.

sentences.zh: 有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 子四人：宗訥、宗誨、宗諤、宗諒。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Zongne, Zonghui, Zonge, and Zongliang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zongne, Zonghui, Zonge, and Zongliang.

sentences.zh: 宗誨，右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Zonghui was Right Director of the Court of Appanages.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui served as right director of the Court of Appanages.

sentences.zh: 宗諒，主賓客員外郎。

translations.literal: Zongliang was Vice Director of the Bureau of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang was vice director of the Bureau of Guests.

sentences.zh: 子 宗訥

translations.literal: Son Zongne
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongne

sentences.zh: 宗訥，字大辨，以蔭補太廟齋郎，遷第四室長。

translations.literal: Zongne, style name Dabian, through inherited privilege was made a qi lang of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was promoted to chief of the fourth chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Zongne, whose style was Dabian, entered service through hereditary privilege as a qi lang of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and rose to chief of the fourth chamber.

sentences.zh: 代謁吏部銓，邊光範意其年少，未能屬辭，語之曰：「苟援筆成六韻詩，雖不試書判，可入等矣。」

translations.literal: Acting for another at the Board of Civil Office selections, Bian Guangfan thought him young and unable to compose documents, and said to him: "If you can take up the brush and complete a regulated verse of six rhymes, even without testing document judgment you may enter the grades."
translations.idiomatic: Substituting at the Board of Civil Office selections, Bian Guangfan thought him too young to write official prose and said, "If you can compose a regulated verse of six rhymes on the spot, you may pass the grade even without the document test."

sentences.zh: 宗訥易之，光範試詩賦，立就。

translations.literal: Zongne readily agreed; Guangfan tested him in poetry and fu, and he finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zongne agreed; Guangfan tested him in poetry and fu, and he finished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂擬授秘書省正字；

translations.literal: The next day he was slated for appointment as collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was slated for appointment as collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又明日，上命擢國子監丞。

translations.literal: The day after that the emperor ordered him promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, the emperor ordered him promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 蓋上居藩邸時，每有篇詠，令昉屬和，前後數百章，皆宗訥繕寫，上愛其楷麗，問知為宗訥所書，故有是命。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been heir apparent he often composed verses and ordered Fang to match them; several hundred chapters in all were copied by Zongne; the emperor loved their regular script and beauty, and learning they were Zongne's hand, gave this order.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, the emperor often composed verses and had Fang match them—several hundred pieces in all, copied out by Zongne. The emperor admired the calligraphy and, learning it was Zongne's hand, issued this order.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，詔賈黃中集《神醫普救方》，宗訥暨劉錫、吳淑、呂文仲、杜鎬、舒雅皆預焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo an edict ordered Jia Huangzhong to compile the Divine Physician's Universal Relief Formulas; Zongne together with Liu Xi, Wu Shu, Lü Wenzhong, Du Gao, and Shu Ya all took part.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo an edict ordered Jia Huangzhong to compile the Divine Physician's Universal Relief Formulas; Zongne joined Liu Xi, Wu Shu, Lü Wenzhong, Du Gao, and Shu Ya in the work.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，昉在相位，上欲命宗訥為尚書郎，昉懇辭，以為非承平故事，止改秘書丞，歷太常博士。

translations.literal: Early in Yongxi, when Fang was chancellor, the emperor wished to appoint Zongne a director in a ministry; Fang earnestly declined, holding that it was not precedent in peaceful times, and he was only changed to secretary and then served through as director of the Court of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi, while Fang was chancellor, the emperor wished to make Zongne a ministry director. Fang declined firmly, saying it was not precedent in settled times; Zongne was made only a secretary, then rose through posts to director of the Court of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宗訥頗習典禮。

translations.literal: Zongne was well versed in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Zongne was well versed in ritual.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，呂端掌禮院，引宗訥同判，累遷比部郎中。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era Lü Duan directed the Court of Ritual and brought Zongne in as associate director; he was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, Lü Duan directed the Court of Ritual and brought Zongne in as associate director; Zongne rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianping he died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 子昭迴，大中祥符五年獻文，召試賜進士第，後為屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhaohui, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu presented a literary work, was summoned for examination and granted the jinshi degree, and later became vice director in the Bureau of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaohui, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, presented a literary work, was examined at court, granted the jinshi degree, and later became vice director in the Bureau of State Farms.

sentences.zh: 昭遜，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Zhaoxun was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxun was palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 子 宗諤

translations.literal: Son Zonge
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zonge

sentences.zh: 宗諤，字昌武，七歲能屬文，恥以父蔭得官，獨由鄉舉，第進士，授校書郎。

translations.literal: Zonge, style name Changwu, at seven could compose literary pieces; ashamed to obtain office through his father's inherited privilege, he entered solely through the provincial examination, ranked as jinshi, and was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge, whose style was Changwu, could compose prose at seven. Ashamed to take office through his father's privilege, he entered by provincial examination alone, passed the jinshi examination, and was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 明年，獻文自薦，遷秘書郎、集賢校理、同修起居注。

translations.literal: The next year he submitted literary works to recommend himself and was moved to secretary, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and co-compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he submitted his own writings in self-recommendation and was promoted to secretary, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and co-compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.

sentences.zh: 先是，後苑陪宴，校理官不與，京官乘馬不得入禁門。

translations.literal: Previously, at banquets in the rear park collator officials did not participate, and capital officials on horseback could not enter the forbidden gates.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, collators had been excluded from banquets in the rear park, and capital officials were not permitted to enter the forbidden gates on horseback.

sentences.zh: 至是，皆因宗諤之請復之，遂為故事。

translations.literal: At this time all were restored through Zonge's request, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On Zonge's petition all these privileges were restored, and the practice became established precedent.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜起居舍人，預重修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed attendant of the Diary of Activity and Repose and took part in the revised compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne, Zonge was appointed attendant of the Diary of Activity and Repose and helped revise the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 從幸大名，上疏曰：「國家馭邊之術，制勝之謀，將帥之短長，兵衛之眾寡，宸算廟謨，盡在吾術中矣。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on an imperial progress to Daming, he submitted a memorial saying: "The state's methods for governing the frontier, plans for victory, generals' strengths and weaknesses, and the numbers of the guard forces—the emperor's calculations and the court's counsels are all within our purview.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor to Daming, he submitted a memorial: "The state's frontier policy, plans for victory, the merits and faults of commanders, and the strength of the armies—the throne's calculations and the court's strategy are all matters we understand.

sentences.zh: 今之言事者，不過請陛下益兵貯糧，分道掩殺，言之甚易，行之則難。

translations.literal: Those who speak on affairs today merely ask Your Majesty to increase troops and store grain and to strike in divided columns—easy to say, hard to do.
translations.idiomatic: Those who advise Your Majesty today ask only for more troops, stored grain, and divided attacks—easily said, but hard to carry out.

sentences.zh: 始受命則無不以攻堅陷陣為壯圖，及遇敵則惟以閉壘塞關為上計，孤君父之重委，致生靈之重困，興言及此，誠可歎息。

translations.literal: When first receiving command none fail to take storming fortified positions as a grand plan, yet on meeting the enemy they take only closing ramparts and blocking passes as the best strategy—betraying the heavy trust of ruler and father and bringing grave distress to the people; to speak of this is truly cause for sighing.
translations.idiomatic: When first appointed, every commander vows to storm walls and break ranks; when the enemy appears, the best plan becomes only to shut the fort and block the passes—betraying the throne's heavy trust and inflicting great suffering on the people. It is truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 自古行軍出師，無不首擇將帥。

translations.literal: Since antiquity in mobilizing armies and going on campaign, none fail first to choose generals.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, no army has marched without first choosing its commanders.

sentences.zh: 夫將帥隨材任使，守一郡，控一城，分領驍勇，爭據要害，又豈直三路主帥之名，然後能制六師生死之命乎？

translations.literal: Generals are appointed according to their talents—holding one commandery, controlling one city, leading the brave in separate forces, striving for key positions—how can only the title of commander of the three frontier circuits then control the life and death of the six armies?
translations.idiomatic: Commanders should be assigned by talent—to hold a prefecture, control a city, lead picked troops, and seize vital ground. Must one bear the title of commander of the three frontier circuits before one can decide whether the armies live or die?

sentences.zh: 今陛下選任非不至也，權位非不重也，告戒非不丁寧也，處置非不專一也；

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's selections are not insufficient, their authority not light, your admonitions not undetailed, your arrangements not undedicated;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's appointments are not lacking, their authority not slight, your warnings not perfunctory, your dispositions not divided;

sentences.zh: 而外敵犯塞，車駕親征，曾不聞出一人一騎為之救助，不知深溝高壘，秣馬厲兵，欲安用哉？

translations.literal: yet when outer enemies violate the frontier and the imperial carriage personally campaigns, one never hears of a single man or horse sent to aid—what use are deep moats, high ramparts, fed horses, and sharpened weapons?
translations.idiomatic: yet when foreign enemies breach the frontier and the emperor himself takes the field, not one man or horse is sent to help. Of what use are deep moats, high walls, fed horses, and sharpened arms?

sentences.zh: 臣以為臨軍易帥，拔卒為將，在此時也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that changing commanders at the front and elevating soldiers to generals—this is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that replacing commanders in the field and promoting soldiers to generalship should be done now.

sentences.zh: 有功者拔於朝，不用者戮於市，亦此時也。

translations.literal: Rewarding merit at court and executing the useless in the marketplace—this too is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Promoting the meritorious at court and executing the worthless in the marketplace should also be done now.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider it.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 然後下哀痛之詔，行蠲復之恩。

translations.literal: Then issue an edict of sorrow and compassion and grant remission and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Then issue an edict of compassion and grant tax remissions and relief.

sentences.zh: 回鸞上都，垂衣當寧，豈不盛哉。」

translations.literal: Return the imperial carriage to the capital, rule at ease upon the throne—would it not be magnificent?"
translations.idiomatic: Return to the capital, rule in tranquil majesty—would that not be glorious?"

sentences.zh: 遷知制誥、判集賢院，纂《西垣集制》，刻石記名氏。

translations.literal: He was moved to drafter of edicts and given charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, compiled the Collected Western Enclosure Edicts, and had names carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of edicts and put in charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, compiled the Collected Western Enclosure Edicts, and had the names inscribed in stone.

sentences.zh: 嘗牒御史臺不平空，中丞呂文仲移文詰之，往復再三。

translations.literal: Once he sent a memorial to the Censorate disputing an unfounded grievance; Vice Censor-in-Chief Lü Wenzhong sent an official letter questioning him, and they exchanged letters repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Once he memorialized the Censorate over a disputed grievance; Vice Censor-in-Chief Lü Wenzhong sent an official inquiry, and they exchanged letters several times.

sentences.zh: 宗諤執言兩省故事與臺司不相統攝者凡八。

translations.literal: Zonge maintained that there were eight precedents in which the Two Departments and the Censorate were not under each other's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge argued that eight established precedents showed the Two Departments and the Censorate were not subject to one another.

sentences.zh: 事聞，卒如宗諤議。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court finally followed Zonge's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, the court adopted Zonge's view.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he was summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he was appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 是秋，將郊，命判太常大樂、鼓吹二署。

translations.literal: That autumn, when the suburban sacrifice was imminent, he was ordered to direct the two offices of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for grand music and for martial music and trumpets.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, with the suburban sacrifice approaching, he was ordered to oversee the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' grand music office and martial music and trumpet office.

sentences.zh: 先是，樂工率以年勞遷補，至有抱其器而不知聲者。

translations.literal: Previously, musicians were generally promoted and appointed according to years of service, so that some held instruments without knowing the sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Previously musicians had usually been promoted on seniority alone, until some carried instruments without knowing how to play them.

sentences.zh: 宗諤素曉音律，遂加審定，奏斥謬濫者五十人。

translations.literal: Zonge had long understood musical pitch and mode, so he added review and verification and memorialized the dismissal of fifty unqualified persons.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge was well versed in music, so he reviewed the roster and memorialized the removal of fifty unqualified musicians.

sentences.zh: 因修完器具，更署職名，條上利病二十事，帝省閱而賞歎之。

translations.literal: He then restored and completed instruments, revised official titles, and submitted a list of twenty items of benefit and harm; the emperor reviewed them and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the instruments, revised the official titles, and submitted twenty recommendations for reform; the emperor read them and commended him.

sentences.zh: 事具《樂志》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully recorded in the Treatise on Music.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in full in the Treatise on Music.

sentences.zh: 又著《樂纂》以獻，命付史館，自是月再肄習焉。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Compendium on Music and presented it; it was ordered deposited in the Historiography Institute, and from then on they rehearsed twice monthly.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Compendium on Music and presented it to the throne; it was deposited in the Historiography Institute, and thereafter rehearsals were held twice each month.

sentences.zh: 時諸神祠壇多闕外壝之制，因深塹列樹以表之，營葺齋室，舊典因以振起。

translations.literal: At the time many spirit-shrine altars lacked the outer enclosure prescribed by ritual, so he dug deep trenches and planted rows of trees to mark them, built and repaired fasting halls, and thereby revived old rites.
translations.idiomatic: Many spirit-shrine altars then lacked the prescribed outer enclosures, so he dug trenches, planted trees to mark the boundaries, and restored the fasting halls, reviving neglected ritual practice.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹遣使來賀承天節，詔宗諤為館伴使，自郊勞至飲餞，皆刊定其儀。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent envoys to congratulate the emperor on his birthday, an edict appointed Zonge host commissioner; from the suburban welcome through the farewell banquet he revised and fixed the ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan envoys came to congratulate the emperor on his birthday, Zonge was appointed host commissioner and standardized the ceremonies from the suburban welcome through the farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，從封泰山，改工部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he accompanied the feng and shan rites at Mount Tai and was changed to director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu he accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai for the feng and shan sacrifices and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 二年，始建昭應宮，命副丁謂為同修宮使。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the Zhaoying Palace was first built, he was ordered to serve as associate commissioner for its construction under Ding Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when construction of the Zhaoying Palace began, he was appointed associate commissioner under Ding Wei.

sentences.zh: 三年，知審官院。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 屬祀汾陰后土，命為經度制置副使，同權河中府事。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice to the earth at Fenyin was undertaken, he was appointed associate commissioner for planning and administration and concurrently given charge of affairs in Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fenyin sacrifice to the earth, he was made associate planning commissioner and concurrently given charge of Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 禮成，優拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was specially promoted to Right Remonstrance and Reform Officer.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites were completed he was specially promoted to right remonstrance and reform officer.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴玉宸殿，上謂曰：「聞卿至孝，宗族頗多，長幼雍睦。

translations.literal: Once while attending a banquet in the Hall of Jade Purity, the emperor said to him: "I have heard that you are deeply filial, that your clan is large, and that elders and juniors live in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending a banquet in the Hall of Jade Purity, the emperor said, "I hear you are deeply filial, that your clan is large, and that young and old live in harmony.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣守二聖基業，亦如卿之保守門戶也。」

translations.literal: In inheriting and guarding the foundations of the two sage emperors, I am also like you in preserving the household."
translations.idiomatic: In inheriting and guarding the legacy of the two sage emperors, I too am like you in keeping the household intact."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「翰林，清華之地，前賢敭曆，多有故事，卿父子為之，必周知也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Hanlin Academy is a place of pure eminence; former worthies who rose through its ranks left many precedents—you and your father served there and must know them well."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added, "The Hanlin Academy is a place of refined distinction; eminent predecessors who passed through it left many precedents—you and your father served there and must know them thoroughly."

sentences.zh: 宗諤嘗著《翰林雜記》以紀國朝制度，明日上之。

translations.literal: Zonge had written the Miscellaneous Hanlin Records to record the dynasty's institutions and presented it the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge had written the Miscellaneous Hanlin Records to record the dynasty's institutions and presented it the next day.

sentences.zh: 宗諤究心典禮，凡創制損益，靡不與聞。

translations.literal: Zonge devoted himself to ritual propriety; in every new institution or revision he had a part.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge devoted himself to ritual; he took part in nearly every new institution or revision.

sentences.zh: 修定皇親故事、武舉武選入官資敘、閣門儀制、臣僚導從、貢院條貫，餘多裁正。

translations.literal: He revised the precedents for imperial clansmen, the qualifications for military-examination appointees, gate-ceremony regulations, the order of procession for officials, and examination-yard rules, and corrected many other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He revised precedents for imperial clansmen, rules for military-examination appointments, gate-ceremony protocol, officials' processional order, and examination regulations, among many other corrections.

sentences.zh: 五年，迎真州聖像，副丁謂為迎奉使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the sacred image was welcomed from Zhenzhou, he served as associate welcoming commissioner under Ding Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the sacred image was welcomed from Zhenzhou, he served as associate welcoming commissioner under Ding Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月，以疾卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he died of illness, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he died of illness at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悼之，謂宰相曰：「國朝將相家，能以聲名自立，不墜門閥，唯昉與曹彬家爾。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned him and said to the chancellor: "Among families of generals and ministers in our dynasty, only those of Fang and Cao Bin have been able to establish reputations by their own merit and not let their house decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and told the chancellor, "Among the great military and ministerial families of our dynasty, only the houses of Fang and Cao Bin have maintained their standing by their own reputations.

sentences.zh: 宗諤方期大用，不幸短命，深可惜也。」

translations.literal: Zonge was just reaching the age of great appointment when, unhappily, his life was cut short—a deep pity."
translations.idiomatic: Zonge was on the verge of great appointment when his life was cut short—it is deeply regrettable."

sentences.zh: 既厚賻其家，以白金賜其繼母，又錄其子若弟以官焉。

translations.literal: He then richly compensated the family, granted silver to his stepmother, and enrolled his sons and younger brothers for office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then granted generous funeral gifts to the family, gave silver to Zonge's stepmother, and enrolled his sons and younger brothers in office.

sentences.zh: 初，昉居三館、兩制之職，宗諤不數年，皆踐其地。

translations.literal: Earlier Fang had held posts in the Three Institutes and the Drafting Office; within a few years Zonge had held them all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang had held posts in the Three Institutes and the Drafting Office; within a few years Zonge had held them all.

sentences.zh: 風流儒雅，藏書萬卷。

translations.literal: Refined and cultivated, he possessed a library of ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated and elegant, he kept a library of ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 內行淳至，事繼母符氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: In private conduct he was pure and sincere; in serving his stepmother, Lady Fu, he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he was utterly sincere; his filial service to his stepmother, Lady Fu, was renowned.

sentences.zh: 二兄早世，奉嫂字孤，恩禮兼盡。

translations.literal: His two elder brothers died early; he served his sister-in-law and honorably cared for the orphans, fulfilling both kindness and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: His two elder brothers died young; he supported his sister-in-law and treated the orphans with full kindness and ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 與弟宗諒友愛尤至，覃恩所及，必先群從，及歿而己子有未仕者。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Zongliang his friendship was especially close; whenever grace was extended he put his kinsmen first, and when he died some of his own sons had not yet received office.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to his younger brother Zongliang; whenever imperial favor was granted he gave priority to his kinsmen, and at his death some of his own sons had still not entered office.

sentences.zh: 程宿早卒，有弟無所依，宗諤為表請於朝而官之。

translations.literal: Cheng Su died early; his younger brother had no one to rely on, and Zonge memorialized the court to appoint him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Su died young, leaving a younger brother with no support; Zonge memorialized the court and had him appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 勤接士類，無賢不肖，恂恂盡禮，獎拔後進，唯恐不及，以是士人皆歸仰之。

translations.literal: He diligently received men of letters; whether worthy or unworthy he treated them with respectful courtesy, encouraged and promoted the young, fearing only that he might not reach them in time—therefore scholars all looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed scholars warmly, treating all with respectful courtesy regardless of rank; he encouraged juniors and feared only that he might not help them enough, and scholars looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 宗諤工隸書。

translations.literal: Zonge was skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Zonge excelled at clerical script.

sentences.zh: 有文集六十卷，《內外制》三十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected works in sixty scrolls and the Inner and Outer Drafts in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in sixty scrolls and the Inner and Outer Drafts in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 嘗預修《續通典》、《大中祥符封禪汾陰記》、《諸路圖經》，又作《家傳》、《談錄》，並行於世。

translations.literal: He helped compile the Continued Comprehensive Institutions, the Record of the Dazhong Xiangfu Feng and Chan at Fenyin, and the Gazetteers of the Various Circuits, and also wrote the Family Biography and the Talks Recorded, all of which circulated widely.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Continued Comprehensive Institutions, the Record of the Dazhong Xiangfu Feng and Chan at Fenyin, and the Gazetteers of the Various Circuits, and also wrote the Family Biography and the Talks Recorded, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子昭遹、昭述、昭適。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhaoyuan, Zhaoshu, and Zhaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhaoyuan, Zhaoshu, and Zhaoshi.

sentences.zh: 孫 昭述

translations.literal: Grandson Zhaoshu
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhaoshu

sentences.zh: 昭述，字仲祖，以父蔭為秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Zhaoshu, style name Zhongzu, through his father's inherited privilege was made collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshu, whose style was Zhongzu, entered service through his father's privilege as collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，賜進士出身，為刑部詳覆官，累遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination at the Academy of Academicians, he was granted jinshi status, became reviewing officer in the Ministry of Justice, and was repeatedly promoted to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Examined at the Academy of Academicians, he was granted jinshi status, appointed reviewing officer in the Ministry of Justice, and rose to secretary.

sentences.zh: 群牧制置使曹利用薦為判官，鄆州牧地侵於民者凡數千頃，昭述悉復之。

translations.literal: Commissioner for Pasturage Cao Li'yong recommended him as administrative aide; several thousand qing of pasturage land in Yan Prefecture had encroached on private holdings, and Zhaoshu restored it all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Li'yong, commissioner for pasturage, recommended him as aide; several thousand qing of Yanzhou pasturage land had encroached on private holdings, and Zhaoshu restored all of it.

sentences.zh: 以太常博士知開封縣，特遷尚書屯田員外郎、開封推官。

translations.literal: As director of the Court of Sacrifices he was made magistrate of Kaifeng County, specially promoted to vice director in the Bureau of State Farms and investigating officer of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Court of Sacrifices he governed Kaifeng County, was specially promoted to vice director in the Bureau of State Farms, and appointed investigating officer of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 坐嘗被曹利用薦，出知常州，遷為三司度支判官，改河北轉運使。

translations.literal: Because he had once been recommended by Cao Li'yong, he was sent out as prefect of Changzhou, then moved to administrative aide in the Finance Commission's budget office and changed to transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been recommended by Cao Li'yong, he was sent out as prefect of Changzhou, then became budget aide in the Finance Commission and transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 江陵屯兵讙言倉粟陳腐，欲以動眾。

translations.literal: The garrison at Jiangling loudly complained that the granary grain was rotten and sought to stir up the troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling the garrison loudly claimed the granary grain was rotten and tried to stir up the troops.

sentences.zh: 昭述取以為奉，且以飯其僚屬，眾遂定。

translations.literal: Zhaoshu took it for his own provisions and also fed his subordinates with it, and the crowd was calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshu ate the grain himself and fed it to his staff as well, and the troops were pacified.

sentences.zh: 徙湖南潭州，戍卒憤監軍酷暴，欲構亂，或指昭述謂曰：「如李公長者，何可負？」

translations.literal: Transferred to Tanzhou in Hunan, the garrison soldiers, angered by the supervising commander's cruelty, wished to plot rebellion; someone pointed to Zhaoshu and said: "How could we betray a worthy like Lord Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Tanzhou in Hunan, the garrison, enraged by their commander's cruelty, plotted mutiny; someone pointed to Zhaoshu and said, "How could we betray a man of integrity like Lord Li?"

sentences.zh: 其謀遂寢。

translations.literal: Their plot then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The plot then collapsed.

sentences.zh: 昭述聞之，以戒監軍。

translations.literal: When Zhaoshu heard of it he used the occasion to admonish the supervising commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoshu learned of this he warned the supervising commander.

sentences.zh: 監軍自是不復為暴。

translations.literal: The supervising commander from then on no longer acted with cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising commander thereafter ceased his abuses.

sentences.zh: 比去，眾遮道羅拜，指妻子曰：「嚮非公，無噍類矣。」

translations.literal: When he was about to leave, the crowd blocked the road and bowed in ranks, pointing to their wives and children and saying: "Had it not been for you, sir, we would have had no one left alive."
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, the people blocked the road and bowed, pointing to their wives and children and saying, "But for you, sir, none of us would be alive."

sentences.zh: 徙淮南轉運使兼發運使，加直史館。

translations.literal: He was moved to transport commissioner of Huainan and concurrently grain-dispatch commissioner, and was given direct appointment in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He became transport commissioner of Huainan and concurrent grain-dispatch commissioner, with direct appointment in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 徙陝西轉運使，糾察在京刑獄，為三司戶部副使，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Moved to transport commissioner of Shaanxi, he inspected capital criminal cases, became vice commissioner of the Finance Commission's household bureau, and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shaanxi transport commissioner, he inspected capital criminal cases, became vice commissioner of the Finance Commission's household bureau, and rose to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 陝西用兵，提點陝西計置糧草，還授度支、鹽鐵副使，以右諫議大夫為河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi was at war he was put in charge of provisioning grain and fodder there; on returning he was appointed vice commissioner of budget and salt and iron, and as Right Remonstrance and Reform Officer became chief transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaanxi campaign he supervised grain and fodder; on his return he became vice commissioner of budget and salt and iron, and as right remonstrance and reform officer was made chief transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 河決澶淵，久未塞。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke its banks at Chanyuan and long remained unsealed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River breached its banks at Chanyuan and remained unsealed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣劉六符來，乃命昭述城澶州，以治堤為名，調兵農八萬，逾旬而就。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent Liu Liufu, Zhaoshu was ordered to fortify Chazhou under the pretext of repairing the dikes; he mobilized eighty thousand soldiers and farmers, and the work was completed in little more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan envoy Liu Liufu arrived, Zhaoshu was ordered to fortify Chazhou under the guise of repairing the dikes; he mobilized eighty thousand soldiers and farmers and finished in little more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 初，六符過之，真以為堤也，及還而城具，甚駭愕。

translations.literal: At first, when Liufu passed by, he truly thought it was only dikes; when he returned the city was complete, and he was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When Liufu first passed through he took it for dike work alone; on his return the city stood complete, and he was deeply astonished.

sentences.zh: 初置義勇軍，人情洶洶，昭述乘疾置日行數舍，開諭父老，眾始安。

translations.literal: When the Righteous and Brave Army was first established public sentiment was turbulent; Zhaoshu, though ill, posted relays and traveled several stops in a day, explaining matters to the elders, and the people were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous and Brave Army was first established, public sentiment was unsettled; though ill, Zhaoshu rode relay horses several stops a day to explain matters to local elders, and the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使表其能，除龍圖閣直學士、知澶州，又為樞密直學士、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner memorialized his ability; he was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Chazhou, then became direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and chief transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner praised his competence; he was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Chazhou, then direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and chief transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 河北始置四路，以為真定府路安撫使、知成德軍。

translations.literal: When the four Hebei circuits were first established he was made pacification commissioner of the Zhending Prefecture circuit and military prefect of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was first divided into four circuits he was made pacification commissioner of the Zhending circuit and military prefect of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 大水，民多流亡，籍僧舍積粟為粥糜，活饑民數萬計。

translations.literal: In a great flood many people fled; he requisitioned grain stored in monasteries to make gruel and porridge and saved tens of thousands of starving people.
translations.idiomatic: During severe flooding many people fled; he requisitioned grain stored in monasteries to make gruel and saved tens of thousands of starving people.

sentences.zh: 改龍圖閣學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: He was changed to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官、御史言昭述庸懦，不可負重鎮，留真定府。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and censorate officials said Zhaoshu was mediocre and timid and could not bear a heavy frontier post, so he was kept at Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and censorate officials said Zhaoshu was mediocre and timid and unfit for a major frontier post, so he remained at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 居四年，入領三班院，以翰林侍讀學士知鄭州。

translations.literal: After four years he entered to head the Three Classes Bureau and, as Hanlin attendant reader, became prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he took charge of the Three Classes Bureau and, as Hanlin attendant reader, became prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知通進銀臺司，判太常寺，復領三班，累遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was made director of the Office for Transmission and Silver Terrace and given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he again headed the Three Classes Bureau and was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became director of the Office for Transmission and Silver Terrace and was put in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he again headed the Three Classes Bureau and rose to right vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 從祫享致齋於朝堂，得暴疾卒。

translations.literal: While observing the fasting rites for the collective sacrifice in the court hall he was seized by sudden illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: While observing the fasting rites for the collective sacrifice in the court hall he was struck by sudden illness and died.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of rites and given the posthumous title Ke.

sentences.zh: 李氏居京城北崇慶里，凡七世不異爨，至昭述稍自豐殖，為族人所望，然家法亦不隳。

translations.literal: The Li clan lived at Chongqing Lane in the north of the capital; for seven generations they did not separate their cooking fires, and by Zhaoshu's time they had grown somewhat prosperous and were looked to by the clan, yet the family rules were not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan lived at Chongqing Lane in the northern capital; for seven generations they shared one kitchen, and though Zhaoshu had brought the family modest prosperity and become the clan's pillar, its rules remained intact.

sentences.zh: 孫 昭遘

translations.literal: Grandson Zhaoyou
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhaoyou

sentences.zh: 昭遘，字逢吉，宗諤從子也，以蔭為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Zhaoyou, style name Fengji, was Zonge's nephew; through inherited privilege he was made chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyou, whose style was Fengji, was Zonge's nephew; through privilege he was made chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction.

sentences.zh: 幼時，楊億嘗過其家，出拜，億命為賦，既成，億曰：「桂林之下無雜木，非虛言也。」

translations.literal: In his youth Yang Yi once visited his home; Zhaoyou came out to pay respects, and Yi ordered him to compose a fu; when it was finished Yi said: "Under the osmanthus grove no miscellaneous trees grow—this is no empty saying."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, when Yang Yi visited his home Zhaoyou came out to greet him; Yi asked him to compose a fu, and when it was done said, "Under the osmanthus grove no miscellaneous trees grow—it is no empty saying."

sentences.zh: 其後薦之，召試，授館閣校勘，改集賢院校理。

translations.literal: Later he recommended him; summoned for examination, he was appointed collator in the palace library and changed to collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi later recommended him; examined at court, Zhaoyou was appointed palace-library collator and then collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 坐失誤落秩。

translations.literal: Because of an error he was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: After an administrative error he was demoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made salt and iron administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as salt and iron administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 初，議罷天下職田及公使錢，昭遘以為不可。

translations.literal: At first, when it was proposed to abolish official fields and public-service funds throughout the empire, Zhaoyou held that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first debated abolishing official fields and public-service funds empire-wide, Zhaoyou argued against it.

sentences.zh: 三司使姚仲孫惡其異己，請詰所以興利之實，昭遘爭不屈，遂罷判官，為白波發運使。

translations.literal: Finance Commissioner Yao Zhongsun, disliking his dissent, asked that the actual profit of his proposals be investigated; Zhaoyou argued without yielding and was therefore removed as administrative aide and made grain-dispatch commissioner on the White River.
translations.idiomatic: Finance Commissioner Yao Zhongsun, resenting his opposition, demanded proof of how his proposals would increase revenue; Zhaoyou refused to yield and was removed as administrative aide and made grain-dispatch commissioner on the White River.

sentences.zh: 因入奏事，仁宗謂曰：「前所論罷職田等事，卿言是也。」

translations.literal: When he entered to report on affairs, Emperor Renzong said to him: "On the earlier matter of abolishing official fields and the like, what you said was correct."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to report on affairs, Emperor Renzong said, "On the earlier proposal to abolish official fields and the like, you were right."

sentences.zh: 遷直史館、知陝州。

translations.literal: He was moved to direct appointment in the Historiography Institute and made prefect of Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was given direct appointment in the Historiography Institute and made prefect of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諫官歐陽修言：「陝府，關中要地，昭遘無治劇材，不宜遣。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance officer Ouyang Xiu said: "Shaan Prefecture is a vital place in the Guanzhong region; Zhaoyou lacks the talent to govern a difficult post and should not be sent there."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officer Ouyang Xiu said, "Shaan Prefecture is a vital point in the Guanzhong region; Zhaoyou lacks the ability to govern a demanding post and should not be sent there."

sentences.zh: 改判三司理欠司，徙度支判官。

translations.literal: He was changed to director of the Finance Commission's office for recovering arrears and moved to budget administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to direct the Finance Commission's office for recovering arrears and made budget administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 使契丹還，道除陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: Returning from an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed on the road as transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed en route transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 坐家僮盜遼人銀酒杯，降知澤州。

translations.literal: Because his household servant stole a Liao man's silver wine cup, he was demoted to prefect of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a household servant stole a Khitan envoy's silver wine cup, he was demoted to prefect of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陽城冶鑄鐵錢，民冒山險輸礦炭，苦其役，為奏罷鑄錢。

translations.literal: At Yangcheng iron cash was cast; the people braved mountain hazards to transport ore and charcoal, suffering under the corvée; he memorialized to abolish coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangcheng iron cash was being cast, and the people, braving mountain hazards to haul ore and charcoal, suffered under the labor; he memorialized to stop the minting.

sentences.zh: 又言：「河東鐵錢真偽淆雜，不可不革。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Hedong, genuine and counterfeit iron cash are mixed together; this cannot go unreformed."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In Hedong genuine and counterfeit iron cash are mingled together, and this must be reformed."

sentences.zh: 後復直史館、知陝州。

translations.literal: Later he again received direct appointment in the Historiography Institute and became prefect of Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again given direct appointment in the Historiography Institute and made prefect of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城中舊無井，唐武德中，刺史長孫操始疏廣濟渠水入城，眾賴其利。

translations.literal: The city had formerly had no wells; in the Wude era of Tang, Prefect Changsun Cao first channeled water from the Guangji Canal into the city, and the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The city had long lacked wells; in the Wude era of Tang, Prefect Changsun Cao first diverted water from the Guangji Canal into the city, and the people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 昭遘至，立廟祠之。

translations.literal: When Zhaoyou arrived, he established a shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoyou arrived, he erected a shrine in Changsun Cao's honor.

sentences.zh: 歸為三司戶部判官，糾察在京刑獄，進直龍圖閣，改集賢殿修撰，累遷尚書工部郎中。

translations.literal: On returning he became administrative aide of the Finance Commission's household bureau, inspected capital criminal cases, was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, changed to compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he became administrative aide of the Finance Commission's household bureau and inspected capital criminal cases; he was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, made compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and rose to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 歷知鳳翔、河中府、晉州，遷管勾登聞檢院。

translations.literal: He successively governed Fengxiang, Hezhong Prefecture, and Jin Prefecture, and was moved to oversee the Appeal and Investigation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Fengxiang, Hezhong Prefecture, and Jin Prefecture, then was put in charge of the Appeal and Investigation Bureau.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、知滄州，用諫官吳及言，復改知陝州，徙鄭州卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Celestial Manifestations and made prefect of Cang Prefecture; on remonstrance officer Wu Ji's advice he was again changed to prefect of Shaan Prefecture, then transferred to Zheng Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Celestial Manifestations and made prefect of Cang Prefecture; on remonstrance officer Wu Ji's recommendation he was again assigned to Shaan Prefecture, then transferred to Zheng Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 昭遘性和易，不忤物，能守家法。

translations.literal: Zhaoyou's nature was easygoing; he did not offend others and was able to uphold the family rules.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyou was easygoing, gave no offense, and upheld the family rules.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正，字聖功，河南人。

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng, style name Shenggong, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng, whose style was Shenggong, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖夢奇，戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mengqi was vice minister of the household bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mengqi was vice minister of the household bureau.

sentences.zh: 父龜圖，起居郎。

translations.literal: His father Qitu was attendant of the diary of activity and repose.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qitu was attendant of the Diary of Activity and Repose.

sentences.zh: 蒙正，太平興國二年，擢進士第一，授將作監丞，通判昇州。

translations.literal: Mengzheng, in the second year of Taiping Xingguo, ranked first among jinshi and was appointed vice director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction and supervising prefect of Sheng Prefecture.
