If Jiqian next spring, before our troops have mobilized, sends troops to rescue Lingwu, drives out all its people, and concentrates his forces in a siege, then the lone city of Ling Prefecture will be hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Now the soldiers and people of Lingwu Army number no less than sixty or seventy thousand, trapped in a place of peril and ruin. If Jiqian next spring, before our troops have mobilized, sends troops to rescue Lingwu, drives out all its people, and concentrates his forces in a siege, then the lone city of Ling Prefecture will be hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 萬一失陷，賊勢益增，縱多聚甲兵，廣積財貨，亦難保必勝矣。

translations.literal: If by any chance it falls, the bandits' strength will increase all the more; even if one gathers many armored troops and amasses vast stores of wealth, it will still be hard to guarantee victory.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance it falls, the enemy's strength will increase all the more; even if many armored troops are gathered and vast stores of wealth amassed, victory will still be hard to guarantee.

sentences.zh: 臣所以乞封潘羅支為六谷王而厚以金帛者，恐繼遷旦暮用兵斷彼賣馬之路也。

translations.literal: The reason I beg to enfeoff Pan Luozhi as King of the Six Valleys and reward him generously with gold and silk is that I fear Jiqian may at any moment use troops to cut off his route for selling horses.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I beg to enfeoff Pan Luozhi as King of the Six Valleys and reward him generously with gold and silk is that I fear Jiqian may at any moment use troops to cut off his route for selling horses.

sentences.zh: 苟朝廷信使得達潘羅支，則泥埋等族、西南遠蕃，不難招集。

translations.literal: If the court's envoys can truly reach Pan Luozhi, then the Niman and other tribes and the distant frontier peoples of the southwest will not be hard to recruit.
translations.idiomatic: If the court's envoys can truly reach Pan Luozhi, then the Niman and other tribes and the distant frontier peoples of the southwest will not be hard to recruit.

sentences.zh: 西南既禀命，而緣邊之勢張，則鄜、延、環、慶之淺蕃，原、渭、鎮戎之熟戶，自然歸化。

translations.literal: Once the southwest has received orders, and the border forces grow strong, then the shallow tribes of Fu, Yan, Huan, and Qing and the registered households of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong will naturally submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once the southwest has received orders and the border forces grow strong, then the shallow tribes of Fu, Yan, Huan, and Qing and the registered households of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong will naturally submit.

sentences.zh: 然後使之與對替甲兵及駐泊軍馬互為聲援，則萬山聞之，必不敢於靈州、河西頓兵矣。

translations.literal: Then have them and the rotating garrison troops and stationed armies mutually support one another, and Wanshan, hearing of it, will certainly not dare to station troops at Ling Prefecture and west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: Then have them and the rotating garrison troops and stationed armies mutually support one another, and Wanshan, hearing of it, will certainly not dare to station troops at Ling Prefecture and west of the River.

sentences.zh: 萬山既退，則賀蘭蕃部亦稍稍叛繼遷矣。

translations.literal: Once Wanshan withdraws, the Helan frontier tribes will also gradually turn against Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wanshan withdraws, the Helan frontier tribes will also gradually turn against Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 若曰名器不可以假人，爵賞不可以濫及，此乃聖人為治之常道，非隨時變易之義也。」

translations.literal: If one says that titles and vessels must not be lent to others and that ranks and rewards must not be bestowed indiscriminately, that is the constant way by which sages govern; it is not the principle of changing with the times."
translations.idiomatic: If one says that titles and honors must not be lent to others and that ranks and rewards must not be bestowed indiscriminately, that is the constant way by which sages govern; it is not the principle of changing with the times."

sentences.zh: 齊賢又請調江淮、荊湘丁壯八萬以益防禦，朝議以為動搖，兼澤國人民，遠戍西鄙亦非便，計遂寢。

translations.literal: Qixian also requested that eighty thousand able-bodied men from the Jianghuai and Jingxiang regions be mobilized to strengthen defenses. Court discussion held that this would cause unrest, and that the people of marsh-and-lake country would also find distant service on the western frontier inconvenient, so the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian also requested that eighty thousand able-bodied men from the Jianghuai and Jingxiang regions be mobilized to strengthen defenses. Court discussion held that this would cause unrest and that marsh-country people would also find distant service on the western frontier inconvenient, so the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 齊賢又言：「靈州斗絕一隅，當城鎮完全、磧路未梗之時，中外已言合棄，自繼遷為患已來，危困彌甚。

translations.literal: Qixian also said: "Ling Prefecture stands utterly isolated in a corner. When its walls were intact and the desert routes unobstructed, both court and countryside already said it ought to be abandoned. Since Jiqian became a threat, its peril has grown ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian also said, "Ling Prefecture stands utterly isolated in a corner. When its walls were intact and the desert routes unobstructed, both court and countryside already said it ought to be abandoned. Since Jiqian became a threat, its peril has grown ever worse.

sentences.zh: 南去鎮戎約五百餘里，東去環州僅六七日程，如此畏途，不須攻奪，則城中之民何由而出，城中之兵何由而歸？

translations.literal: South to Zhenrong is about five hundred li or more; east to Huan Prefecture is only six or seven days' journey. On such a fearful road, unless it is taken by assault, how can the people in the city get out, and how can the soldiers in the city return?
translations.idiomatic: South to Zhenrong is about five hundred li or more; east to Huan Prefecture is only six or seven days' journey. On such a fearful road, unless the city is taken by assault, how can the people inside get out and how can the soldiers inside return?

sentences.zh: 欲全軍民，理須應接。

translations.literal: To preserve both army and people, one must by principle provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve both army and people, relief must by principle be provided.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，若能增益精兵，以合西邊屯駐、對替之兵，從以原、渭、鎮戎之師，率山西熟戶從東界而入，嚴約師期，兩路交進。

translations.literal: The plan for the present is this: if elite troops can be increased and combined with the garrison and rotating troops stationed on the western border, together with the armies of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, leading registered households west of the mountains to enter from the eastern frontier, setting a strict date for the campaign, and advancing by two routes together—
translations.idiomatic: The plan for the present is this: if elite troops can be increased and combined with the garrison and rotating troops stationed on the western border, together with the armies of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, leading registered households west of the mountains to enter from the eastern frontier, setting a strict date for the campaign, and advancing by two routes together—

sentences.zh: 設若繼遷分兵以應敵，我則乘勢而易攻。

translations.literal: then if Jiqian divides his troops to meet the enemy, we can seize the opportunity and attack where it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: then if Jiqian divides his troops to meet the enemy, we can seize the opportunity and attack where it is easy.

sentences.zh: 且奔命途道，首尾難衛，千里趨利，不敗則禽。

translations.literal: Moreover, rushing to obey orders over long distances makes it hard to guard both head and tail; racing a thousand li for gain, if one is not defeated one is captured.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, rushing to obey orders over long distances makes it hard to guard both head and tail; racing a thousand li for gain, if one is not defeated one is captured.

sentences.zh: 臣謂兵鋒未交，而靈州之圍自解。

translations.literal: I say that before the armies clash, the siege of Ling Prefecture will resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: I say that before the armies clash, the siege of Ling Prefecture will resolve itself.

sentences.zh: 然後取靈州軍民，而置砦於蕭關、武延川險要處以僑寓之，如此則蕃漢士人之心有所依賴。

translations.literal: Then take the soldiers and people of Ling Prefecture and establish stockades at strategic points such as Xiaoguan and Wuyanchuan to lodge them temporarily; in this way the hearts of frontier Chinese and tribal people will have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Then take the soldiers and people of Ling Prefecture and establish stockades at strategic points such as Xiaoguan and Wuyanchuan to lodge them temporarily; in this way the hearts of frontier Chinese and tribal people will have something to rely on.

sentences.zh: 裁候平寧，卻歸舊貫，然後縱蕃漢之兵，乘時以為進退，則成功不難矣。」

translations.literal: Wait only until peace is restored, then return them to their former places; then release frontier Chinese and tribal troops to advance and withdraw as opportunity allows, and success will not be hard."
translations.idiomatic: Wait only until peace is restored, then return them to their former places; then release frontier Chinese and tribal troops to advance and withdraw as opportunity allows, and success will not be hard."

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，靈武果陷。

translations.literal: Before long Lingwu indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lingwu indeed fell.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月，拜右僕射、判邠州，不行，改判永興軍兼馬步軍部署。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month he was appointed Right Vice Director and assigned to Bin Prefecture, but did not go; he was changed to serve as prefect of Yongxing Army and concurrent Horse and Foot Deployment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month he was appointed right vice director and assigned to Bin Prefecture, but did not go and was instead made prefect of Yongxing Army and concurrent horse and foot deployment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時薛居正子惟吉妻柴氏無子早寡，盡畜其貨產及書籍論告，欲改適齊賢。

translations.literal: At the time the wife of Xue Juzheng's son Weiji, Lady Chai, was childless and had long been a widow; she gathered all her property and books and brought suit, wishing to remarry Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the wife of Xue Juzheng's son Weiji, Lady Chai, was childless and had long been a widow. She gathered all her property and books and brought suit, wishing to remarry Qixian.

sentences.zh: 惟吉子安上訴其事，上不欲置於理，命司門員外郎張正倫就訊，柴氏所對與安上狀異。

translations.literal: Weiji's son Anshang appealed the matter. The emperor did not wish to put it before the law and ordered Supervisory Gate Outer Official Zhang Zhenlun to investigate on the spot; Lady Chai's answers differed from Anshang's petition.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji's son Anshang appealed the matter. The emperor did not wish to put it before the law and ordered Supervisory Gate Outer Official Zhang Zhenlun to investigate on the spot; Lady Chai's answers differed from Anshang's petition.

sentences.zh: 下其事於御史，乃齊賢子太子中舍宗誨教柴氏為詞。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the censorate, and it turned out that Qixian's son, Crown Prince Household Aide Zong Hui, had coached Lady Chai in her testimony.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the censorate, and it turned out that Qixian's son, crown prince household aide Zong Hui, had coached Lady Chai in her testimony.

sentences.zh: 齊賢坐責太常卿、分司西京，宗誨貶海州別駕。

translations.literal: Qixian was punished by being demoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and commissioner in the Western Capital; Zong Hui was demoted to Vice Prefect of Hai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian was punished by being demoted to director of the court of imperial sacrifices and commissioner in the Western Capital; Zong Hui was demoted to vice prefect of Hai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景德初，起為兵部尚書、知青州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era he was recalled and made Minister of War and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde era he was recalled and made minister of war and prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上幸澶淵，命兼青、淄、濰州安撫使。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Chanyuan, Qixian was ordered to serve concurrently as Commissioner for Appeasement of Qing, Zi, and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Chanyuan, Qixian was ordered to serve concurrently as commissioner for appeasement of Qing, Zi, and Wei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was changed to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上疏言曰：「 臣在先朝，常憂靈、夏，兩鎮終為繼遷並吞，言事者以臣所慮為太過，略舉既往之事以明本末。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "When I was at the previous court I often feared that Ling and Xia, the two garrisons, would in the end be swallowed up by Jiqian. Those who spoke on affairs thought my concern excessive. Let me briefly cite past events to show cause and effect.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "When I was at the previous court I often feared that the Ling and Xia garrisons would in the end be swallowed up by Jiqian. Those who spoke on affairs thought my concern excessive. Let me briefly cite past events to show cause and effect.

sentences.zh: 當時臣下皆以繼遷只是懷戀父祖舊地，別無他心，先帝與以銀州廉察，庶滿其意。

translations.literal: At that time all officials below thought Jiqian only longed for his father and grandfather's old lands and had no other intent; the previous emperor gave him the prefectural commission of Yin Prefecture, hoping this would satisfy him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all officials below thought Jiqian only longed for his father and grandfather's old lands and had no other intent; the previous emperor gave him the prefectural commission of Yin Prefecture, hoping this would satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 爾後攻劫不已，直至降麟、府州界八部族蕃酋，又脅制賀蘭山下帳族，言事者猶謂封獎未厚。

translations.literal: Afterward he raided without cease, until he subjugated the eight tribal chieftains of the Lin and Fuzhou border region and coerced the encampment tribes beneath Helan Mountain; those who spoke on affairs still said the enfeoffment and rewards had not been generous enough.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he raided without cease, until he subjugated the eight tribal chieftains of the Lin and Fuzhou border region and coerced the encampment tribes beneath Helan Mountain; those who spoke on affairs still said the enfeoffment and rewards had not been generous enough.

sentences.zh: 洎陛下賜以銀、夏土壤，寵以節旄，自此姦威愈滋，逆志尤暴。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty granted him the lands of Yin and Xia and honored him with a military commission, from that time his treacherous power grew ever stronger and his rebellious intent became all the more violent.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty granted him the lands of Yin and Xia and honored him with a military commission, from that time his treacherous power grew ever stronger and his rebellious intent became all the more violent.

sentences.zh: 屢斷靈州糧路，復撓緣邊城池，數年之間，靈州終為吞噬。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he cut Ling Prefecture's grain routes and again harassed the border cities; within several years Ling Prefecture was at last swallowed up.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he cut Ling Prefecture's grain routes and again harassed the border cities; within several years Ling Prefecture was at last swallowed up.

sentences.zh: 當靈池、清遠軍垂欲陷沒，臣方受經略之命。

translations.literal: When Lingchi and Qingyuan Army were on the verge of falling, I had just received appointment as frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingchi and Qingyuan Army were on the verge of falling, I had just received appointment as frontier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 臣思繼遷須是得一兩處強大蕃族與之為敵，此乃以蠻夷攻蠻夷，古今之上策也。

translations.literal: I thought Jiqian must be given one or two powerful frontier tribes as enemies; this is using barbarians to attack barbarians—the supreme strategy of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: I thought Jiqian must be given one or two powerful frontier tribes as enemies; this is using barbarians to attack barbarians—the supreme strategy of antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 遂請以六谷名目封潘羅支，俾其展效。

translations.literal: I therefore requested that Pan Luozhi be enfeoffed under the title of the Six Valleys, so that he might show results.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore requested that Pan Luozhi be enfeoffed under the title of the Six Valleys so that he might show results.

sentences.zh: 其時近臣所見，全與臣謀不同，多為沮撓。

translations.literal: At that time the views of close ministers were entirely unlike my plan, and most obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the views of close ministers were entirely unlike my plan, and most obstructed it.

sentences.zh: 及繼遷為潘羅支射殺，邊患謂可少息。

translations.literal: When Jiqian was shot and killed by Pan Luozhi, the border trouble was thought able to subside somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian was shot and killed by Pan Luozhi, the border trouble was thought able to subside somewhat.

sentences.zh: 今其子德明依前攻劫，析逋遊龍缽等盡在部下，其志又似不小。

translations.literal: Now his son Deming raids as before; Xibo, Youlongbo, and the like are all under his command, and his ambition again seems no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Now his son Deming raids as before; Xibo, Youlongbo, and the like are all under his command, and his ambition again seems no small matter.

sentences.zh: 臣慮德明乘大駕東幸之際，去攻六谷，則瓜、沙、甘、肅、于闐諸處漸為控制矣。

translations.literal: I fear Deming may take advantage of the great procession's eastern journey to attack the Six Valleys, and then Gua, Sha, Gan, Su, and Khotan and other places will gradually come under his control.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Deming may take advantage of the great procession's eastern journey to attack the Six Valleys, and then Gua, Sha, Gan, Su, Khotan, and other places will gradually come under his control.

sentences.zh: 向使潘羅支尚在，則德明未足為虞；

translations.literal: If Pan Luozhi had still been alive, then Deming would not have been worth worrying about;
translations.idiomatic: If Pan Luozhi had still been alive, then Deming would not have been worth worrying about;

sentences.zh: 今潘羅支已亡，廝鐸督恐非其敵。

translations.literal: now that Pan Luozhi is dead, Siduodu probably cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: now that Pan Luozhi is dead, Siduodu probably cannot match him.

sentences.zh: 望委大臣經制其事。」

translations.literal: I hope a chief minister may be entrusted to manage this affair."
translations.idiomatic: I hope a chief minister may be entrusted to manage this affair."

sentences.zh: 從東封還，復拜右僕射。

translations.literal: Returning from the eastern fengshan ceremony, he was again appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the eastern fengshan ceremony, he was again appointed right vice director.

sentences.zh: 時建玉清昭應宮，齊賢言繪畫符瑞，有損謙德，又違奉天之意，屢請罷其役。

translations.literal: At the time the Yujing Zhaoying Palace was being built. Qixian said that painting auspicious omens would impair modest virtue and also violate the intent of the fengshan at Mount Tai; he repeatedly requested that the work be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Yujing Zhaoying Palace was being built. Qixian said that painting auspicious omens would impair modest virtue and also violate the intent of the fengshan at Mount Tai, and repeatedly requested that the work be stopped.

sentences.zh: 三年，出判河陽，從祀汾陰還，進左僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out to serve as prefect of Heyang; returning from attendance at the fengshan at Fenyin, he was promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out to serve as prefect of Heyang; returning from attendance at the fengshan at Fenyin, he was promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 五年，代還，請老，以司空致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his term as replacement ended, he requested retirement and retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when his term as replacement ended, he requested retirement and retired as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 入辭便坐，方拜而仆，上遽止之，許二子扶掖升殿，命益坐茵為三。

translations.literal: Entering to take leave at the informal audience seat, just as he bowed he collapsed. The emperor hastily stopped him, permitted his two sons to support him up the steps, and ordered an additional seat cushion, making three.
translations.idiomatic: Entering to take leave at the informal audience seat, just as he bowed he collapsed. The emperor hastily stopped him, permitted his two sons to support him up the steps, and ordered an additional seat cushion, making three.

sentences.zh: 歸洛，得裴度午橋莊，有池榭松竹之盛，日與親舊觴詠其間，意甚曠適。

translations.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he obtained Pei Du's Wuchao estate, with pools, pavilions, pines, and bamboo in great abundance; day after day he drank and composed poetry there with relatives and old friends, his mood very free and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Luoyang, he obtained Pei Du's Wuchao estate, with pools, pavilions, pines, and bamboo in great abundance. Day after day he drank and composed poetry there with relatives and old friends, his mood very free and at ease.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，薨，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, summer, he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, in summer, he died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Education and given the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed minister of education and given the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 齊賢姿儀豐碩，議論慷慨，有大略，以致君自負。

translations.literal: Qixian's bearing was imposing and his physique large; his discourse was passionate and he had broad strategy, taking upon himself the task of bringing the ruler to sagehood.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian's bearing was imposing and his physique large; his discourse was passionate and he had broad strategy, taking upon himself the task of bringing the ruler to sagehood.

sentences.zh: 留心刑獄，多所全活。

translations.literal: He devoted attention to criminal cases and preserved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted attention to criminal cases and preserved many lives.

sentences.zh: 喜提獎寒雋。

translations.literal: He delighted in promoting talented men of humble origin.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in promoting talented men of humble origin.

sentences.zh: 少時家貧，父死無以為葬，河南縣吏為辦其事，齊賢深德之，事以兄禮，雖貴不替也。

translations.literal: In youth his family was poor; when his father died there was no means for burial, and a clerk of Henan County arranged the funeral. Qixian was deeply grateful and treated him with the courtesy due an elder brother; even when exalted he did not change this.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his family was poor; when his father died there was no means for burial, and a clerk of Henan County arranged the funeral. Qixian was deeply grateful and treated him with the courtesy due an elder brother; even when exalted he did not change this.

sentences.zh: 仲兄昭度嘗授齊賢經，及卒，表贈光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: His second elder brother Zhaodu had once taught Qixian the classics; when he died, Qixian memorialized to have him posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His second elder brother Zhaodu had once taught Qixian the classics; when he died, Qixian memorialized to have him posthumously granted vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又嘗依太子少師李肅家，肅死，為營葬事，歲時祭之。

translations.literal: He had also once relied on the household of Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince Li Su; when Su died, Qixian arranged his burial and sacrificed to him at the seasonal festivals.
translations.idiomatic: He had also once relied on the household of Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince Li Su; when Su died, Qixian arranged his burial and sacrificed to him at the seasonal festivals.

sentences.zh: 趙普嘗薦齊賢於太宗，未用，普即具前列事，以謂：「陛下若進齊賢，則齊賢他日感恩，更過於此。」

translations.literal: Zhao Pu once recommended Qixian to Taizong, but he was not employed. Pu then fully set forth the foregoing matters, saying: "If Your Majesty advances Qixian, then Qixian's gratitude in days to come will exceed even this."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu once recommended Qixian to Taizong, but he was not employed. Pu then fully set forth the foregoing matters, saying, "If Your Majesty advances Qixian, then Qixian's gratitude in days to come will exceed even this."

sentences.zh: 上大悅，遂大用。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and then employed him on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and then employed him on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 种放之起，齊賢所薦也。

translations.literal: Zhong Fang's rise to office was through Qixian's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Fang's rise to office was through Qixian's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 齊賢四踐兩府，九居八座，以三公就第，康寧福壽，時罕其比。

translations.literal: Qixian four times tread the two departments and nine times occupied one of the eight chief seats; he retired to his estate as one of the Three Dukes, enjoying health, peace, good fortune, and long life—rarely matched in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian four times tread the two departments and nine times occupied one of the eight chief seats; he retired to his estate as one of the three dukes, enjoying health, peace, good fortune, and long life—rarely matched in his time.

sentences.zh: 居相日，數起大獄，又與寇準相傾，人或以此少之。

translations.literal: While chief minister he several times initiated major prosecutions and also contended with Kou Zhun; some for this reason thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: While chief minister he several times initiated major prosecutions and also contended with Kou Zhun; some for this reason thought somewhat less of him.

sentences.zh: 齊賢諸子皆能有立：宗信，內殿崇班；

translations.literal: All of Qixian's sons were able to establish themselves: Zongxin, Inner Hall Honored Officer;
translations.idiomatic: All of Qixian's sons were able to establish themselves: Zongxin, Inner Hall Honored Officer;

sentences.zh: 宗理，大理寺丞；

translations.literal: Zongli, aide of the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: Zongli, aide of the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 宗諒，殿中丞；

translations.literal: Zongliang, palace aide;
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang, palace aide;

sentences.zh: 宗簡，閣門祗候；

translations.literal: Zongjian, Ceremonial Gateway Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian, Ceremonial Gateway Attendant;

sentences.zh: 宗訥，太子中舍；

translations.literal: Zongne, Crown Prince Household Aide;
translations.idiomatic: Zongne, Crown Prince Household Aide;

sentences.zh: 宗禮最賢，雖累資登朝，而畏羈束，故多居田里。

translations.literal: Zong Li was the most worthy; though he repeatedly rose by seniority to court office, he feared restraint and therefore mostly lived in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Li was the most worthy; though he repeatedly rose by seniority to court office, he feared restraint and therefore mostly lived in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 子 宗誨

translations.literal: Son Zong Hui
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zong Hui

sentences.zh: 宗誨，字習之，齊賢第二子也。

translations.literal: Zong Hui, courtesy name Xizhi, was Qixian's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hui, courtesy name Xizhi, was Qixian's second son.

sentences.zh: 少喜學兵法，陰陽、象緯之書無不通究。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in studying military methods and thoroughly mastered books on yin and yang, astronomy, and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he delighted in studying military methods and thoroughly mastered books on yin and yang, astronomy, and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭為秘書省正字，遷至太子中舍，貶海州別駕。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he became a proofreader in the Secretariat and rose to Crown Prince Household Aide; he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Hai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he became a proofreader in the Secretariat and rose to crown prince household aide; he was demoted to vice prefect of Hai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗通判河陽，徙知富順監。

translations.literal: He once served as transit judge of Heyang and was transferred to serve as superintendent of Fushun Superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as transit judge of Heyang and was transferred to serve as superintendent of Fushun Superintendency.

sentences.zh: 會夷人斗郎春叛，群獠皆騷動，宗誨將郡兵攻破之。

translations.literal: When the Yi tribesman Doulangchun rebelled and all the mountain tribes were disturbed, Zong Hui led the prefectural troops and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yi tribesman Doulangchun rebelled and all the mountain tribes were disturbed, Zong Hui led the prefectural troops and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 擢開封府判官、三司度支勾院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judicial administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture and review officer of the Fiscal Affairs Commission of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture and review officer of the fiscal affairs commission of the three departments.

sentences.zh: 宗誨在開封日，御史王沿劾其嗜酒廢事，及為河北轉運使，乃發沿居喪假官舟賈販，朝論惡之。

translations.literal: While Zong Hui was at Kaifeng, Censor Wang Yan impeached him for loving wine and neglecting duties; when he became transport commissioner of Hebei, he then exposed that Yan, while in mourning, had used an official boat for trade. Court opinion despised this.
translations.idiomatic: While Zong Hui was at Kaifeng, Censor Wang Yan impeached him for loving wine and neglecting duties; when he became transport commissioner of Hebei, he then exposed that Yan, while in mourning, had used an official boat for trade. Court opinion despised this.

sentences.zh: 會以調發擾民，徙知徐州。

translations.literal: When his mobilization of labor disturbed the people, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mobilization of labor disturbed the people, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿，後為永興軍兵馬鈐轄，又徙鄜延路兼知鄜州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, later served as Military Controller of Yongxing Army, and was again transferred to Fuyan Circuit with concurrent service as prefect of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices, later served as military controller of Yongxing Army, and was again transferred to Fuyan Circuit with concurrent service as prefect of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇延安，劉平、石元孫敗沒，鈐轄黃德和遁還，延州不納，又走鄜州。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao raided Yan'an; Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated and perished; the qianxia Huang Dehe fled back; Yan Prefecture would not admit him, and he fled again to Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao attacked Yan'an, Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated and killed. The qianxia Huang Dehe fled back, but Yan Prefecture refused to receive him, and he fled on to Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宗誨曰：「軍奔將無所歸，激之則為亂矣。」

translations.literal: Zonghui said: "When fleeing troops and their general have nowhere to return, if provoked they will become rebellious."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui said, "When routed soldiers and their commander have nowhere to go, stirring them up will only make them rebel."

sentences.zh: 乃納之，拘德和以聞。

translations.literal: He then admitted them, detained Dehe, and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore admitted them, detained Dehe, and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 是時鄜城不完，且無備，傳言寇兵至，人心不安。

translations.literal: At that time Fu city was incomplete and unprepared; rumors spread that enemy troops had arrived, and the people were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the walls of Fu were unfinished and the city was unprepared. When word spread that enemy troops were approaching, the populace grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 宗誨乃嚴斥候，籍入而禁出，使老幼倂力守禦之，敵亦自引去。

translations.literal: Zonghui then strictly posted scouts, registered those entering and forbade exit, had old and young together exert strength to defend, and the enemy also withdrew on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui then tightened the scouts, registered entrants and barred departures, and had young and old alike join in the defense. The enemy withdrew of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 領興州防禦使，復徙永興鈐轄兼知邠州，以秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: He held the post of Defender of Xing Prefecture, was again transferred to be qianxia of Yongxing while also governing Bin Prefecture, and retired as Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Defender of Xing Prefecture, was later transferred to qianxia of Yongxing while also governing Bin Prefecture, and finally retired with the rank of Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 嘗事干謁，其子曰：「昔賀秘監以道士服東歸會稽，明皇賜以鑒湖，以為休老之地。

translations.literal: Once engaged in calling and paying visits; his son said: "In old times Supervising Secretary He returned east to Kuaiji in Taoist robes; Emperor Ming of Tang granted him Mirror Lake as a place to retire and rest.
translations.idiomatic: He had once busied himself with calls and visits. His son said, "Long ago Supervising Secretary He returned east to Kuaiji dressed as a Taoist, and Emperor Ming of Tang granted him Mirror Lake as a place to spend his old age in peace.

sentences.zh: 今洛下雖無鑒湖，而嵩、少、伊，天下佳處，雖非朝廷所賜，皆閑逸之人所有爾。

translations.literal: Now though Luoyang lacks Mirror Lake, Song, Shao, and Yi are the finest places under heaven; though not granted by the court, they all belong to people at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Today Luoyang may lack Mirror Lake, but Song, Shao, and Yi are among the finest places in the realm. Though the court did not grant them, they are all held by men who live at ease.

sentences.zh: 大人盍衣羽服以優遊，何必更事請謁乎？」

translations.literal: Why does the Elder not don feather robes to roam freely—why must you again attend to calling and visiting?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not put on Taoist robes and wander freely? Why must you go on calling and paying visits?"

sentences.zh: 宗誨曰：「吾作白頭老監秘書而眠，何以賀老流沙之服為哉？」

translations.literal: Zonghui said: "I sleep as a white-haired old supervising secretary—why should I wear Old He's robes of flowing sand?"
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui replied, "I am content to sleep out my days as a white-haired old supervising secretary. Why should I wear Old He's flowing-sand robes?"

sentences.zh: 時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time this was considered a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was regarded as a memorable remark.

sentences.zh: 初，齊賢守代州，宗誨嘗預計畫，其保任親族不問疏近，以年為先後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qixian was governor of Dai Prefecture, Zonghui had participated in planning; in recommending relatives he made no distinction of near or distant, taking age as the order.
translations.idiomatic: When Qixian had earlier served as governor of Dai Prefecture, Zonghui had taken part in his planning. In recommending relatives he made no distinction between close and distant kin, ordering them only by age.

sentences.zh: 然性貪，雖謝事，猶事貨殖，以至於卒。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was greedy; though he had resigned office, he still engaged in trade and profit-making until his death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy by nature. Even after leaving office he continued to pursue trade and profit until he died.

sentences.zh: 子二人。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 子皋，字叔謨，少有才名而不自負，人樂與之遊。

translations.literal: Zi Gao, style Shumo, in youth had a reputation for talent yet was not self-important; people delighted in associating with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Gao, whose style was Shumo, won a name for talent in his youth but was never self-important, and people were glad to keep his company.

sentences.zh: 最善尹洙，洙曰：「吾交天下士多矣，不以通否易意者，子皋也。」

translations.literal: He was closest to Yin Zhu; Zhu said: "I have associated with men of talent throughout the realm; the one who does not change his attitude according to success or failure is Zi Gao."
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to Yin Zhu, who said, "I have known men of talent throughout the realm, but the one who never alters his regard according to success or failure is Zi Gao."

sentences.zh: 舉進士，試秘書郎、知新鄭縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was tried as Secretary Lang, and governed Xinzheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served probation as a secretary, and was appointed magistrate of Xinzheng County.

sentences.zh: 以齊賢相，遷校書郎，館閣獻頌，擢著作佐郎，進直史館，累官至尚書司封員外郎。

translations.literal: Because Qixian was chancellor, he was promoted to Proofreader; he submitted panegyrics to the institutes, was elevated to Assistant Compiler, advanced to duty in the History Institute, and by accumulated ranks reached Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Qixian became chancellor, he was promoted to proofreader. He submitted panegyrics to the palace institutes, was raised to assistant compiler, entered regular duty at the History Institute, and eventually rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 子憲，字彥章，以蔭將作監主簿，以獻文賜同進士出身，累遷尚書刑部郎中、知光化軍。

translations.literal: Zi Xian, style Yanzhang, through inherited privilege became chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings; through submitting prose he was granted jinshi status by imperial favor; by accumulation he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice and governed Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xian, whose style was Yanzhang, entered service through inherited privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. After submitting a literary work he was granted jinshi standing by imperial favor, and by successive promotions he became Director in the Ministry of Justice and military prefect of Guanghua.

sentences.zh: 戍卒逐其帥韓綱，餘黨作亂，子憲招降之。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers drove out their commander Han Gang; the remnant faction stirred up trouble, and Zi Xian won them over and received their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison soldiers expelled their commander Han Gang, and the remaining ringleaders rose in revolt. Zi Xian persuaded them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 征稅重，人多逋負，子憲奏除之。

translations.literal: Taxes were heavy and many people were in arrears; Zi Xian memorialized to remit them.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were heavy and many people had fallen into arrears. Zi Xian memorialized for their remission.

sentences.zh: 歷太常少卿、三司鹽鐵判官、直史館、知洪州。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Rites, judge of the Salt and Iron Commission of the Three Offices, on duty in the History Institute, and governor of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Rites, judge of the Salt and Iron Commission, on duty at the History Institute, and prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫、知桂州，不赴，御史劾之，降秘書監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor and made governor of Gui Prefecture; he did not go; censors impeached him and he was demoted to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor and appointed prefect of Guizhou, but he did not take up the post. Censors impeached him, and he was demoted to Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 復為光祿卿，加直秘閣、知廬州，遷秘書監，累職徙揚州，卒。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of Imperial Entertainments, added duty in the Secret Archive and governance of Lu Prefecture, promoted to Secretary Director, by accumulated posts transferred to Yang Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as Director of Imperial Entertainments, given concurrent duty in the Secret Archive and appointment as prefect of Luzhou, promoted to Secretary Director, and after further transfers ended as prefect of Yangzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 賈黃中

translations.literal: Jia Huangzhong
translations.idiomatic: Jia Huangzhong

sentences.zh: 賈黃中，字媧民，滄州南皮人，唐相耽四世孫。

translations.literal: Jia Huangzhong, style Huamin, was a man of Nanpi in Cang Prefecture, fourth-generation descendant of Tang chancellor Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Huangzhong, whose style was Huamin, came from Nanpi in Cang Prefecture and was a fourth-generation descendant of the Tang chancellor Jia Dan.

sentences.zh: 父玭，字仲寶，晉天福三年進士，解褐。

translations.literal: His father Bin, style Zhongbao, passed the jinshi in the third year of Tianfu of Jin and received his first appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bin, whose style was Zhongbao, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Tianfu era of Jin and entered official service.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為刑部郎中，終水部員外郎、知浚儀縣，年七十卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was Director in the Ministry of Justice; he ended as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and governor of Junyi County, dying at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice. He ended his career as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and magistrate of Junyi County, and died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 玭嚴毅，善教子，士大夫子弟來謁，必諄諄誨誘之。

translations.literal: Bin was stern and resolute, skilled at teaching his children; when sons of scholar-officials came to visit, he invariably instructed and guided them with earnest care.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was stern and resolute and skilled in educating his children. Whenever the sons of scholar-officials came to visit, he always counseled and guided them with patient earnestness.

sentences.zh: 初，通判鎮州，葬鄉黨群從之未葬者十五喪，孤貧不自給者，咸教育而婚嫁之。

translations.literal: In his early career as vice-prefect of Zhen Prefecture, he buried fifteen unburied coffins of clan fellows in his village community; those orphaned and poor who could not support themselves, he all educated and saw married.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career, while serving as vice-prefect of Zhen Prefecture, he buried fifteen unburied coffins among his kinsmen in the village. Orphans and the poor who could not support themselves he educated and saw properly married.

sentences.zh: 黃中幼聰悟，方五歲，比每旦令正立，展書卷比之，謂之「等身書」，課其誦讀。

translations.literal: Huangzhong was clever from childhood; when he was just five, Bin each morning had him stand straight, unrolled book scrolls to measure against him, called it "body-length books," and tested his recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was bright from childhood. When he was only five, Bin had him stand upright each morning, unrolled book scrolls to measure against his height, called them "body-length books," and tested his recitation.

sentences.zh: 六歲舉童子科，七歲能屬文，觸類賦詠。

translations.literal: At six he was presented for the boys' examination; at seven he could compose prose and compose verses on whatever subject arose.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was entered for the boys' examination, and at seven he could compose prose and write verses on whatever theme was set before him.

sentences.zh: 父常令蔬食，曰：「俟業成，乃得食肉。」

translations.literal: His father often had him eat vegetables, saying: "Wait until your studies are complete—only then may you eat meat."
translations.idiomatic: His father often made him eat vegetables, saying, "Wait until your studies are complete; only then may you eat meat."

sentences.zh: 十五舉進士，授校書郎、集賢校理，遷著作佐郎、直史館。

translations.literal: At fifteen he passed the jinshi, was appointed Collator and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and was promoted to Assistant Compiler and duty in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator and proofreader at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and was promoted to assistant compiler with duty at the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，遷左拾遺，歷左補闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was promoted to Left Reminder and served successively as Left Complementer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianlong era he was promoted to Left Reminder and later served as Left Complementer.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，通判定州，判太常禮院。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao he was vice-prefect of Ding Prefecture and concurrently judged the Ritual Court of the Grand Ceremonies Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Kaibao era he served as vice-prefect of Ding Prefecture and concurrently adjudicated the Ritual Court of the Grand Ceremonies Commission.

sentences.zh: 黃中多識典故，每詳定禮文，損益得中，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Huangzhong knew many precedents and old regulations; each time he scrutinized and fixed ritual texts, his additions and subtractions hit the mean, and he was praised as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong knew a great many institutional precedents. Whenever he scrutinized and revised ritual texts, his additions and deletions struck the proper balance, and he was praised as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，以黃中為采訪使，廉直平恕，遠人便之。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified, Huangzhong was made touring commissioner; upright, fair, and lenient, remote people found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingnan was pacified, Huangzhong was appointed touring commissioner. Upright, fair, and lenient, he made things easier for the people of the distant south.

sentences.zh: 還奏利害數十事，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized on several tens of matters of advantage and harm, all meeting imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted memorials on several dozen matters of public benefit and harm, all of which met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 會克江表，選知宣州。

translations.literal: When the Jiang region was conquered, he was selected to govern Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiang region was conquered, he was chosen to serve as prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，民多為盜，黃中出己奉造糜粥，賴全活者以千數，仍設法弭盜，因悉解去。

translations.literal: In a year of famine many people became bandits; Huangzhong spent his own salary to make gruel; those preserved alive numbered in the thousands; he also devised methods to quell banditry, and thus all were released.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year many people turned to banditry. Huangzhong spent his own salary to prepare gruel, saving thousands of lives. He also devised measures to suppress robbery, and in the end all the offenders were released.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，知昇州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he governed Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Taiping Xingguo era he was appointed prefect of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時金陵初附，黃中為政簡易，部內甚治。

translations.literal: At that time Jinling had only recently submitted; Huangzhong's governance was simple and easy, and within his jurisdiction there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jinling had only recently submitted to the dynasty. Huangzhong governed with simplicity and ease, and his jurisdiction was very well ordered.

sentences.zh: 一日，案行府署中，見一室扃鑰甚固，命發視之，得金寶數十匱，計直數百萬，乃李氏宮閣中遺物也，即表上之。

translations.literal: One day as he made an inspection tour of the prefectural offices, he saw a room locked very securely; he ordered it opened and inspected, finding several tens of chests of gold and jewels worth several million, the leftover possessions of the Li court palace—he immediately memorialized and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while inspecting the prefectural offices, he noticed a room locked with unusual care. He ordered it opened and found several dozen chests of gold and jewels worth millions—the leftover treasures of the Li palace. He immediately memorialized and surrendered them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上覽表謂侍臣曰：「非黃中廉恪，則亡國之寶，將汙法而害人矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and told attending ministers: "Were it not for Huangzhong's integrity and restraint, the treasures of a perished state would have stained the law and harmed people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and told his attending ministers, "Had Huangzhong not been upright and scrupulous, the treasures of a fallen dynasty would have corrupted the law and brought harm to the people."

sentences.zh: 賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: He was granted three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was granted three hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起復視事。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his father, he was recalled from mourning to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 五年，召歸闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有薦黃中文學高第，召試中書，拜駕部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Huangzhong's literary learning as top rank; he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Chariots and entrusted with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended Huangzhong's literary attainments as outstanding. He was summoned for examination at the Secretariat and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Chariots with responsibility for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 八年，與宋白、呂蒙正等同知貢舉，遷司封郎中，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Song Bai and Lü Mengzheng he jointly supervised the civil examinations; he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served with Song Bai and Lü Mengzheng as joint supervisor of the civil examinations, was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was appointed a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，又知貢舉，俄掌吏部選。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he again supervised the examinations; soon he took charge of selections in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongxi era he again supervised the examinations, and soon afterward took charge of personnel selections in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was added as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era he was additionally appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year he was additionally made compiler of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was also made compiler of the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 凡再典貢部，多柬拔寒俊，除擬官吏，品藻精當。

translations.literal: In all he twice presided over the examinations; he often selected and promoted men of talent from humble backgrounds; in appointing and nominating officials, his judgments were precise and apt.
translations.idiomatic: In all he twice presided over the examination bureau. He often selected talented men from humble backgrounds, and in recommending and appointing officials his judgments were precise and apt.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年秋，與李沆並拜給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Chunhua he and Li Kan were together appointed Supervising Censor and Vice Director of the Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of the Chunhua era he and Li Kan were jointly appointed Supervising Censor and Vice Director of the Administration.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見其母王氏，命坐，謂曰：「教子如是，真孟母矣。」

translations.literal: Taizong summoned his mother Lady Wang, ordered her seated, and said: "To teach a son thus—truly a Mencius's mother."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned his mother, Lady Wang, had her seated, and said, "To raise a son like this is truly the work of a Mencius's mother."

sentences.zh: 作詩以賜之，頒賜甚厚。

translations.literal: He composed a poem to bestow on her, and grants were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a poem to bestow upon her and granted her lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 黃中素重呂端為人，屬端出鎮襄陽，黃中力薦於上，因留為樞密直學士，遂參知政事。

translations.literal: Huangzhong had always valued Lü Duan's character; when Duan was sent out to govern Xiangyang, Huangzhong strongly recommended him to the emperor, and Duan was kept as direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and thus became Vice Director of the Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong had always admired Lü Duan's character. When Duan was sent out to govern Xiangyang, Huangzhong strongly recommended him to the throne. Duan was retained as direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and thus became Vice Director of the Administration.

sentences.zh: 當世文行之士，多黃中所薦引，而未嘗言，人莫之知也。

translations.literal: Literary and upright men of the age were mostly introduced by Huangzhong, yet he never spoke of it—people did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the leading literary and upright men of the age owed their advancement to Huangzhong's recommendations, yet he never spoke of it, and people did not know.

sentences.zh: 然畏慎過甚，中書政事頗留不決。

translations.literal: Yet he was excessively cautious and fearful; at the Secretariat, affairs were often held back undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was excessively cautious and apprehensive, and at the Secretariat many affairs were left undecided.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，與沆並罷守本官。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourth year he and Kan were together dismissed and kept their original ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he and Li Kan were both dismissed from the administration and retained their original ranks.

sentences.zh: 明年，知襄州，上言母老乞留京，改知澶州。

translations.literal: The next year he governed Xiang Prefecture; he memorialized that his mother was old and begged to remain in the capital; he was changed to govern Chan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou. He memorialized that his mother was old and begged to remain in the capital, and was reassigned as prefect of Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辭日，上戒之曰：「夫小心翼翼，君臣皆當然；

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience, the emperor admonished him: "To be cautious and apprehensive—both ruler and minister should be so;
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his farewell audience, the emperor admonished him, "To be cautious and apprehensive is right for both ruler and minister;

sentences.zh: 若太過，則失大臣之體。」

translations.literal: if it goes too far, one loses the bearing of a great minister."
translations.idiomatic: but if it goes too far, one loses the bearing proper to a great minister."

sentences.zh: 黃中頓首謝。

translations.literal: Huangzhong prostrated himself and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong prostrated himself and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 上因謂侍臣曰：「朕嘗念其母有賢德，七十餘年未覺老，每與之語，甚明敏。

translations.literal: The emperor then told attending ministers: "I have often thought his mother possesses virtuous character; for more than seventy years she has not seemed old; each time I speak with her she is very bright and keen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told his attending ministers, "I have often reflected that his mother is a woman of virtue. Though more than seventy, she does not seem old, and whenever I speak with her she is remarkably clear-minded.

sentences.zh: 黃中終日憂畏，必先其母老矣。」

translations.literal: Huangzhong is apprehensive all day long—surely he puts his mother's age first."
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong lives in constant apprehension—surely because he puts his mother's age first."

sentences.zh: 因目參知政事蘇易簡曰：「易簡之母亦如之。

translations.literal: He then looked at Vice Director Su Yijian and said: "Yijian's mother is also like this.
translations.idiomatic: He then looked at Vice Director Su Yijian and said, "Yijian's mother is much the same.

sentences.zh: 自古賢母不可多得。」

translations.literal: From antiquity worthy mothers have been hard to find in plenty."
translations.idiomatic: Worthy mothers have always been hard to find."

sentences.zh: 易簡前謝曰：「陛下以孝治天下，獎及人親，臣實何人，膺茲榮遇。」

translations.literal: Yijian stepped forward and thanked him: "Your Majesty governs the realm with filial piety and rewards even others' parents—what sort of person am I to receive such honored favor?"
translations.idiomatic: Yijian stepped forward and thanked him, "Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety and extends reward even to others' parents. What sort of man am I to receive such an honor?"

sentences.zh: 至道初，黃中遘疾，詔令歸闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao Huangzhong fell ill; an edict ordered him to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao era Huangzhong fell ill, and an edict ordered him to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會建儲宮，擇大臣有德望者為賓友，黃中在選中。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent's palace was established, great ministers of virtue and reputation were chosen as his companions; Huangzhong was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent's palace was established, eminent ministers of virtue and standing were chosen as his companions, and Huangzhong was among those selected.

sentences.zh: 以久疾，改命李至、李沆兼賓客，黃中亦特拜禮部侍郎，代至兼秘書監。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged illness, Li Zhi and Li Kan were instead appointed as companions; Huangzhong was also specially promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, replacing Zhi while also holding Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his long illness, Li Zhi and Li Kan were instead appointed companions to the heir apparent. Huangzhong was specially promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, replacing Li Zhi while also serving as Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 黃中素嗜文籍，既居內閣，甚以為慰。

translations.literal: Huangzhong had always loved books and records; once he held a post in the inner cabinet, he took great consolation in it.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong had always loved books and records, and once he held a post in the inner cabinet he found great satisfaction in it.

sentences.zh: 二年，以疾卒，年五十六，其母尚無恙，卒如上言。

translations.literal: In the second year he died of illness at age fifty-six; his mother was still well—he died just as he had said above.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died of illness at the age of fifty-six. His mother was still in good health, and he died just as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上聞其素貧，別賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor heard he had always been poor and separately granted three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that he had always lived in poverty, the emperor separately granted three hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 既葬，其母入謝，又賜白金三百兩。

translations.literal: After the burial his mother came in to give thanks and was again granted three hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial his mother came to court to give thanks and was granted a further three hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 上謂之曰：「勿以諸孫為念，朕當不忘也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to her: "Do not worry about your grandsons—I shall not forget them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to her, "Do not worry about your grandsons. I shall not forget them."

sentences.zh: 黃中端謹，能守家法，廉白無私。

translations.literal: Huangzhong was upright and careful, able to uphold his family's standards, pure and without private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was upright and careful, upheld his family's standards, and was incorruptible and without private interest.

sentences.zh: 多知臺閣故事，談論亹亹，聽者忘倦焉。

translations.literal: He knew many precedents of the central offices; his discourse was fluent and unceasing, and listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He knew a great many precedents of the central offices. His conversation was fluent and inexhaustible, and listeners forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 在翰林日，太宗召見，訪以時政得失，黃中但言：「臣職典書詔，思不出位，軍國政事，非臣所知。」

translations.literal: During his days in the Hanlin, Taizong summoned him and inquired about the gains and losses of current policy; Huangzhong only said: "Your subject's duty is to preside over documents and edicts; my thoughts do not go beyond my office—military and state affairs are not what your subject knows."
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Hanlin Academy, Huangzhong was summoned by Taizong and asked about the strengths and weaknesses of current policy. Huangzhong replied only, "Your subject's duty is to manage documents and edicts. My thoughts do not go beyond my office, and military and state affairs are not matters I know."

sentences.zh: 上益重之，以為謹厚。

translations.literal: The emperor valued him all the more, considering him cautious and solid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued him all the more and regarded him as cautious and dependable.

sentences.zh: 及知政事，卒無所建明，時論不之許。

translations.literal: When he served in the administration, in the end he proposed nothing noteworthy, and contemporary opinion did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the administration, however, he ultimately offered no notable initiatives, and contemporary opinion did not approve of him.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子守謙，雍熙二年進士；

translations.literal: His son Shouqian passed the jinshi in the second year of Yongxi;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouqian passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Yongxi era;

sentences.zh: 守正，獻文召試，賜進士第，後為虞部員外郎；

translations.literal: Shouzheng, through submitting prose was summoned for examination and granted jinshi rank, later becoming Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzheng, after submitting a literary work, was summoned for examination and granted jinshi standing, and later became Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works;

sentences.zh: 守約，國子博士；

translations.literal: Shouyue, national university erudite;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue, an erudite of the National University;

sentences.zh: 守文，殿中丞；

translations.literal: Shouwen, palace aide;
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen, a palace aide;

sentences.zh: 守訥，右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Shoune, Right Officer of Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: and Shoune, Right Officer of Goodness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《詩》云：「允也天子，降予卿士，實為阿衡，實左右商王。」

translations.literal: Commentary says: The Odes says: "Truly this Son of Heaven, Heaven sends down to him ministers—truly to be the Aheng, truly to assist the King of Shang."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The Odes states, "Truly this Son of Heaven—Heaven sends down to him ministers, truly to be the Aheng, truly to assist the King of Shang."

sentences.zh: 言有是君則有是臣，有是臣則足以相是君也。

translations.literal: It means: when there is such a ruler, there are such ministers; when there are such ministers, they suffice to assist such a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This means that when there is such a ruler, there will be such ministers; and when there are such ministers, they will suffice to assist such a ruler.

sentences.zh: 太宗勵精庶政，注意輔相，以昉舊德，亟加進用，繼擢蒙正、齊賢，迭居相位；

translations.literal: Taizong applied himself zealously to governance, paid attention to chief ministers—because Fang was an elder of virtue he was promptly promoted and employed; then Mengzheng and Qixian were raised in succession, alternating in the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong applied himself zealously to governance and paid close attention to his chief ministers. Because Li Fang was a man of long-standing virtue, he was promptly promoted and employed; Lü Mengzheng and Zhang Qixian were then raised in succession and alternated in the chancellorship;

sentences.zh: 復進黃中，俾參大政。

translations.literal: then Huangzhong was advanced to participate in great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and Huangzhong was later advanced to participate in great affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 而四臣者將順德美，修明庶政，以致承平之治，可謂君臣各盡其道者矣。

translations.literal: These four ministers accommodated and followed virtue and excellence, clarified and improved common governance, and thereby brought about the rule of sustained peace—one may say ruler and ministers each fulfilled their proper way.
translations.idiomatic: These four ministers supported their ruler's virtue, refined ordinary governance, and thereby brought about an age of sustained peace. One may say that ruler and ministers each fulfilled their proper role.

sentences.zh: 君子謂李昉為多遜所毀而不校，蒙正為張紳所汙而不辨，齊賢為同列所累而不言，黃中多所薦引而不有其功，此固人之所難也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen say Li Fang was slandered by Duoxun yet did not contend; Mengzheng was defiled by Zhang Shen yet did not argue; Qixian was burdened by colleagues yet did not speak; Huangzhong recommended many yet did not claim the credit—these are indeed what people find hard.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment say that Li Fang was slandered by Lu Duoxun yet did not contend with him; Lü Mengzheng was maligned by Zhang Shen yet did not defend himself; Zhang Qixian was wronged by colleagues yet did not protest; and Jia Huangzhong recommended many men yet never claimed the credit. These are things people find hard to do.

sentences.zh: 而況四臣者皆賢宰輔，又能進退有禮，皆以善終，非盛德君子，其孰能與於斯？

translations.literal: Moreover, the four ministers were all worthy chief ministers, and also able to advance and withdraw with propriety, all ending well—if not gentlemen of supreme virtue, who could join in this?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, all four were worthy chief ministers who knew how to advance and withdraw with propriety and all ended their lives well. If they were not men of the highest virtue, who could have achieved such a record?
